This breaks all consumers using bun build --compile (e.g. Tauri app sidecars). The regression was introduced in 0.2.96 and does not exist in 0.2.91. The package files list also omits tempfile.js.
signals.review_reason: Build-breaking regression: any consumer using bun build --compile is completely blocked after upgrading to 0.2.96. The published npm artifact is incomplete — a file referenced by another shipped file is absent. Users must pin to an older version to unblock their build pipeline.

source_issues.title: Regression in 0.2.96: bun --compile fails due to missing ./tempfile.js import target
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction steps provided. Error: 'Could not resolve: "./tempfile.js"' in extractFromBunfs.js. tempfile.js is missing from package contents and files list. Rolling back to 0.2.91 restores success. Affects Tauri app sidecar builds.

signals.topic: ExitWorktree fails across separate query() calls with same session ID
signals.summary: When a worktree is created via EnterWorktree in one query() call and the same session ID is used in a subsequent query() call, ExitWorktree fails with 'no active EnterWorktree session'. The worktree state is lost between separate query() invocations even when session ID is preserved. Users cannot implement multi-turn worktree workflows across separate query() calls.
aliases: EnterWorktree state not persisted across query() calls
worktree session state lost between sessions
signals.review_reason: Key workflow breakage: users rely on EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree for safe branch isolation. When the session state is lost between query() calls, users cannot properly clean up worktrees, leading to orphaned branches and directories. The commit message in the SDK itself confirms this is a known regression.

source_issues.title: ExitWorktree claims "no active EnterWorktree session" if worktree created in earlier query()
source_issues.evidence: Full repro with minimal example. SDK returns 'no active EnterWorktree session to exit' error when ExitWorktree is called in a separate query() with the same session ID. Related commit 5a75d29 explicitly acknowledges 'EnterWorktree state lost across query() calls'. External repro repo provided.

signals.topic: MCP server processes become zombies after session ends
signals.summary: When using the relay pattern (looping query() calls), MCP server processes spawned internally by each session survive after the session ends. These zombie processes accumulate over time (5-10 sessions → dozens of zombie processes), consuming memory and causing potential port conflicts. No mechanism exists to associate MCP PIDs with sessions for cleanup.
aliases: MCP processes not cleaned up on session end
signals.review_reason: Operational resource leak: zombie MCP processes accumulate over time in relay/orchestration patterns, causing memory bloat and potential port conflicts. The workaround of PID diffing is fragile and breaks for concurrent missions. This is a systemic resource management failure in a core usage pattern (relay orchestrator).

source_issues.title: query(): MCP server processes remain as zombies after session ends
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 relay orchestrator with MCP Memory and MCP RAG servers. After 5-10 sessions, dozens of zombie node.exe/python.exe processes accumulate. External PID diff workaround breaks for concurrent missions. Full impact analysis: memory consumption, port conflicts.

signals.topic: Bun runtime crashes on startup with 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json', blocking Claude Code from running
signals.summary: Bun internal error 'directory mismatch for directory .../tsconfig.json' causes Claude Code process to exit with code 1 immediately on startup, across multiple runner images and action versions. Same action SHA succeeds at one time and crashes at another on identical runner images, indicating a non-deterministic Bun file-descriptor race condition.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Claude Code 进程在启动时即崩溃，完全无法运行。覆盖 ubuntu-22.04 和 ubuntu-24.04 多个 action 版本，且相同 action SHA 在相同 runner 镜像上时而成功时而失败，说明是 Bun 运行时文件描述符竞态问题，非配置错误。

source_issues.title: Consistent Bun crash: 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' — Claude Code process exits with code 1
source_issues.evidence: Consistent crash on ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-22.04 across multiple action versions (v1.0.92, v1.0.90, v1.0.89, pinned SHA). Same action SHA succeeds at 22:22 UTC but crashes at 23:03 UTC on same runner image 20260406.80.1. 4 failed run links provided. Bun exits with code 1 before any API call is made.

source_issues.title: Claude Code Action won't run due to 'app token exchange' GitHub App installation token (HTTP 401 Unauthorized)
source_issues.evidence: Also shows Bun internal error 'directory mismatch for directory .../tsconfig.json' in the same run. The user installed the action via Claude Code's slash command and it fails to run.

signals.topic: v1.0.90 breaks Bedrock SigV4 authentication — SDK sends bare base64 instead of AWS-signed request, causing 403 errors
signals.summary: After v1.0.90 update, Bedrock users' AWS SigV4 signing chain broke: the Authorization header sends a bare base64 string instead of properly formatted AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 credentials, causing 403 errors on all Bedrock workflows. Pinning to v1.0.89 is the workaround.
aliases: Bedrock SDK falls back to non-Bedrock client
Bedrock AWS credentials chain broken v1.0.90
signals.review_reason: v1.0.90 发布后所有 Bedrock 用户工作流立即阻断，SDK 错误地使用普通 Anthropic 客户端而非 Bedrock 客户端，导致 403。同一 action 版本前后只差 17 分钟即从成功变为失败，根因明确。两条独立 issue 证明影响范围不限于单一用户。

source_issues.title: v1.0.90 breaks Bedrock auth with OIDC-assumed AWS credentials
source_issues.evidence: v1.0.90 released 2026-04-08 04:42 UTC breaks Bedrock auth with 403 SigV4 signing error for OIDC-assumed AWS credentials. Authorization header contains raw base64 hash instead of AWS SigV4 format. Pinning to v1.0.89 resolves. 2 failed run links provided.

source_issues.title: Bedrock SigV4 authentication broken after v1.0.90 (Claude Code 2.1.96 / Agent SDK 0.2.96)
source_issues.evidence: After v1 tag updated to v1.0.90 at 04:43 UTC, Authorization header sends bare base64 instead of AWS SigV4 format. SDK appears to use regular Anthropic client instead of Bedrock client despite use_bedrock:'true'. Multiple workflow types affected (auto-triage, code-review). Success at 04:42, failure at 04:59 — 17-minute window between working and broken. Workaround: pin to v1.0.89.

signals.topic: GitHub App token exchange fails with 401 Unauthorized, blocking action authentication
signals.summary: App token exchange fails with 401 Unauthorized after 3 retries when the action runs in GitHub Actions, preventing all authenticated operations.
signals.review_reason: 认证失败导致 action 完全无法运行，用户设置了 API key 仍无效，说明不是配置问题而是 token exchange 机制本身的问题。但仅单条 issue 且无其他用户佐证，定为 P2。

source_issues.title: Claude Code Action won't run due to 'app token exchange' GitHub App installation token (HTTP 401 Unauthorized)
source_issues.evidence: App token exchange failed: 401 Unauthorized - Failed to get GitHub App installation token after 3 retries. User's Claude Code setup installed via Claude Code's slash command fails to run entirely. User tried setting Anthropic API Key as repo variable with no effect.

signals.topic: PR #1174 adds .husky to SENSITIVE_PATHS, breaking pre-commit hooks in repos that rely on npx husky hook installation
signals.summary: PR #1174 added .husky to SENSITIVE_PATHS, causing the action to restore/reset the .husky directory. Repos that commit .husky files but rely on 'npx husky' to install the actual hook setup have their pre-commit hooks wiped after the action runs.
signals.review_reason: 明确的回归性问题：PR #1174 引入，导致用户的 git hooks 在 action 运行后失效，核心功能受损。但仅单条 issue，无高频证据，定为 P2。

source_issues.title: Adding .husky to SENSITIVE_PATHS breaks repos that commit .husky files but not the hook setup
source_issues.evidence: PR #1174 added .husky to SENSITIVE_PATHS. After this change, pre-commit hooks no longer run because the hook setup is wiped and would need to be reinstalled via 'npx husky'. Regression from previous behavior where .husky was not treated as sensitive.

signals.topic: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when SENSITIVE_PATHS entries are symlinks — action fails to restore config on symlink-using repos
signals.summary: Since v1.0.89, the action crashes during restoreConfigFromBase when any SENSITIVE_PATHS entry (e.g. CLAUDE.md) is a symlink. cpSync tries to recreate the symlink but the parent directory doesn't exist yet.
signals.review_reason: action 在特定文件结构（symlink）下崩溃，是 PR #1174 引入的回归，直接影响该类用户的配置恢复流程。仅单条 issue，定为 P2。

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Since v1.0.89, action crashes during restoreConfigFromBase with ENOENT: no such file or directory, symlink. cpSync in restore-config.ts defaults to dereference:false, tries to recreate symlink but parent dir doesn't exist. Introduced in PR #1174 (same PR that added .husky regression). Workaround: pin to v1.0.88.

signals.topic: Agent tool not available to sub-agents — prevents orchestrator/multi-agent pattern
signals.summary: Sub-agents spawned via the Agent tool do not receive the Agent tool in their own toolset, even with 'All tools' specified. This completely blocks the 'agent of agents' orchestrator pattern.
signals.review_reason: Core workflow blocking: the orchestrator pattern (sub-agent spawning sub-agents) is a documented, expected use case that is completely prevented. Three independent spawn methods all fail with clear evidence. Even though count=1, the impact is a fundamental architectural capability being unavailable — equivalent to 'key feature unusable' per pain point definition.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Agent tool not available to sub-agents — prevents orchestrator pattern
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct spawn methods all tested and failed: foreground teammate (team_name set) — 'Teammates cannot spawn other teammates'; foreground inline (no team_name) — Cannot call Agent(); background (run_in_background: true) — no Agent, no TeamCreate, no SendMessage, no Task tools. Sub-agents get Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, SendMessage, TeamCreate, TaskCreate, MCP tools but NOT Agent. Blocks the core 'agent of agents' design pattern.

signals.topic: Model provider switch resets all conversation context and memory state
signals.summary: Switching between model providers mid-session causes complete loss of conversation history, memory files, and in-progress understanding. No handoff occurs.
aliases: context not preserved on model change
signals.review_reason: High-impact workflow disruption: users on multi-provider setups (cost optimization, A/B testing) cannot switch models mid-session without losing ALL session state. Forces an unnatural 'write before switch' discipline that breaks conversation flow. Documented as a regression in context handoff behavior between provider sessions.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Model provider switch resets conversation context and memory state
source_issues.evidence: Switching models mid-session causes complete loss of: .claude/learnings/ and MEMORY.md entries, conversation history, in-progress findings, tool use memory. Forces fragile workaround: users must write all critical findings to MEMORY.md before any switch or lose them permanently. Breaks multi-provider cost optimization and model routing workflows entirely.

signals.topic: Local token estimation diverges from API-reported tokens for cached context — causes unexpected context overruns
signals.summary: Claude Code's local token estimation does not correctly account for cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens, causing the context bar and AutoCompact threshold to be wildly inaccurate.
aliases: AutoCompact fires at wrong threshold due to cache tokens
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact: users relying on local token estimation for context management get surprised with unexpected API limit hits and potential for data loss when AutoCompact fires too late. The inaccuracy is quantified (100K cache tokens unaccounted), making this a concrete, reproducible billing risk.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Token estimation vs API-reported tokens diverge significantly for cached context
source_issues.evidence: A session with 100K cache_read_input_tokens may show as '60% full' locally while actually consuming far more of the API's context budget. AutoCompact fires at wrong threshold (too late or too early). Context bar shows misleading percentage. Users unexpectedly hit API limits when local estimation showed headroom. Root cause: getEffectiveContextWindowSize() does not correctly subtract cache fields from effective window.

signals.topic: Cache read tokens from parallel subagent dispatch accumulate multiplicatively without bound — causes runaway billing
signals.summary: Each parallel subagent independently re-reads full conversation history from cache, accumulating cache_read tokens multiplicatively on the parent session with no deduplication or cap.
aliases: subagent cache tokens inflate parent bill
multiplicative cache read cost from parallel agents
signals.review_reason: Clear, quantified cost loss: 15M cache_read tokens in a single 90-minute session is a concrete financial harm. This is not a feature gap — the current behavior causes unexpected, unbounded billing that users cannot predict or control. The parent session is billed for subagent overhead it shouldn't bear.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Cache read tokens from parallel subagent dispatch accumulate without upper bound
source_issues.evidence: Spawning 3 parallel subagents causes 3x the cache reads billed to parent session. A 90-minute parallel subagent session can burn ~15M cache_read tokens with no user benefit. Subagent cache reads should not inflate parent session costs. Documented formula: 3 agents x N context tokens each = 3N cache reads. No deduplication, no cap.

signals.topic: Context window detection fails for third-party Anthropic-compatible providers — AutoCompact misfires
signals.summary: Claude Code only detects context window size for api.anthropic.com, falling back to 200K default for all third-party providers (MiniMax, Azure, Bedrock, etc.), causing AutoCompact to trigger at ~19% of actual window.
aliases: AutoCompact fires too early for MiniMax
max_input_tokens detection blocked for non-Anthropic providers
signals.review_reason: Key functionality impaired for third-party provider users: AutoCompact triggers far too early, wasting context efficiency. Users hit manual /compact necessity when auto-compact should have fired correctly. While count=1, the issue affects all users of non-Anthropic providers (Azure, AWS Bedrock, Vertex, MiniMax, OpenRouter) — a broad class of users.

source_issues.title: Context window detection fails for third-party Anthropic-compatible providers
source_issues.evidence: isFirstPartyAnthropicBaseUrl() gates getModelCapability(), causing MiniMax and all non-anthropic URLs to fall through to MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT = 200_000. For a model supporting 1M tokens served via MiniMax, AutoCompact threshold is set at 187K (93.5% of 200K) instead of ~950K (95% of 1M) — firing at ~19% of actual window. Root cause in src/utils/model/modelCapabilities.ts:46-51.

signals.topic: LLM-based grading example false positive due to substring matching bug
signals.summary: The `grade_completion` function in the LLM-based grading documentation example uses `"correct" in grader_response.lower()` which incorrectly evaluates "incorrect" as "correct" since "correct" is a substring of "incorrect", causing all answers to be graded as correct.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete functional bug with fully reproducible steps. The grading function silently returns incorrect results (every answer graded as 'correct') with no error indication, breaking the core evaluation workflow. Users relying on this cookbook example for automated test evaluation will get false 100% pass rates.

source_issues.title: [BUG] False positive in LLM-based grading example
source_issues.evidence: Bug report provides exact reproduction steps showing that when grader outputs 'incorrect', the substring check 'correct' in 'incorrect' evaluates to True, resulting in 100% score even with wrong golden answers. The grading logic silently returns wrong results with no error.

signals.topic: security-guidance JS-only rules fire false positives on Python, Markdown, YAML and other non-JS files, blocking Write/Edit operations
signals.summary: The security-guidance plugin's substring-based rules (child_process_exec, react_dangerously_set_html, document_write_xss, innerHTML_xss, new_function_injection) apply without any file-extension guard, causing them to fire on Python, Markdown, YAML, and other non-JS files that happen to contain the same substrings. This blocks legitimate Write/Edit operations.
aliases: security hook fires on non-JS files
signals.review_reason: Direct workflow blocking in polyglot codebases. Two independent reporters confirm the same root cause: JS-specific substring rules fire without file-type awareness. #1341 explicitly documents 2h of wasted engineering time and a 150-line workaround script. #1329 shows the pattern is pervasive (exec( fires on every Python file). This makes the security-guidance plugin actively harmful to polyglot workflows.

source_issues.title: security-guidance: JS-only rules fire on Python/Markdown/YAML files (file-extension guard missing)
source_issues.evidence: Writing Python SQLAlchemy file with db_session.execute(...) was blocked (JS child_process_exec fires on 'exec('). Writing markdown memo was blocked. An agent spent ~2h writing a 150-line workaround script to evade detection.

source_issues.title: Security Guidance: substring-based rules fire false positives on docs, configs, and non-JS source files
source_issues.evidence: exec( substring is worst offender: every .py file in Python codebases using SQLModel triggers the warning. Due to dedup logic, first write of any new file is blocked with exit code 2. Pickle substring fires on any README mentioning pickle. Agent wasted time working around the false positive.

signals.topic: ralph-loop shell command permission check repeatedly fails, blocking the skill from running
signals.summary: The ralph-loop skill's shell command invocation contains a backtick-wrapped multiline shell command that triggers a permission check failure in Claude Code's security model. This is a recurring issue spanning multiple reported instances and PR attempts.
aliases: ralph-loop permission gate blocks skill invocation
signals.review_reason: High-impact: skill is completely unusable due to permission check failure. Cross-session leakage evidence (#1319) shows users suffered hundreds of wasted conversation turns before noticing. The issue has persisted across at least 5 prior attempts at fix, indicating structural complexity. Both inbound and outbound directions of ralph-loop are compromised.

source_issues.title: (ralph-loop) Error: Shell command permission check failed for pattern
source_issues.evidence: Error: Shell command permission check failed for pattern '```! ...```': This command requires approval. Previously reported in #50, #67, #69, #91; fixed but never merged in #72, #98, #117, #151, #1314.

signals.topic: Discord plugin Bun server process orphaned on Windows after Claude Code session closes
signals.summary: The --shell=bun indirection in the MCP launch command creates a process chain where Claude Code only kills its direct child, leaving the grandchild Bun server process running as an orphan. The Discord bot remains online and responds with emoji reactions but cannot send text replies.
signals.review_reason: User-visible process orphaning creates a degraded bot state where the Discord bot appears partially functional (emoji reactions work) but core text reply capability is absent. This misleads users into thinking the bot is working when it's actually in a broken half-state. Also a resource leak on Windows.

source_issues.title: Discord plugin: bun server.ts orphaned on Windows after Claude Code session closes
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, closing Claude Code leaves bun server.ts running as orphan. Bot stays online in Discord, reacts with emoji but cannot send text replies. Confirmed by reporter. Issue was closed but with no evidence of fix merge.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin inbound messages consumed but never rendered as Claude Code user turns
signals.summary: The Telegram MCP server polls and consumes inbound messages from Telegram but they never appear in the Claude Code session as <channel source='telegram'> user turns. Outbound reply works fine. The inbound direction is completely non-functional.
aliases: telegram notifications not showing in session
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure: the Telegram channel integration is half-broken. Users can send outbound messages but cannot receive inbound messages in the Claude Code session. The core two-way channel communication pattern is broken, defeating the purpose of the integration.

source_issues.title: telegram@0.0.4: inbound messages consumed by server but never rendered as <channel> tag in Claude Code session
source_issues.evidence: Telegram bot successfully polls messages but <channel source='telegram'> tag never appears in CC session. User cannot receive messages from Telegram contacts inside the Claude Code workflow. Outbound works; inbound completely broken. Diagnosis shows mcp.notification fires but harness never renders it.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin creates duplicate Bun poller processes causing noticeable background CPU churn and 409 Conflict errors
signals.summary: When marketplace and cache copies of the plugin are both loaded, duplicate Bun processes compete for the same Telegram bot token. Telegram only allows one getUpdates consumer per token, causing 409 Conflict errors and continuous retry/wake cycles that produce significant CPU consumption even when the plugin appears idle.
signals.review_reason: Visible resource consumption issue: users observe unexplained CPU churn when the plugin should be idle. The 409 Conflict errors from duplicate polling can also cause message delivery failures. This is a known recurring pattern per the related issue cross-references.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: duplicate pollers cause background CPU churn even when idle
source_issues.evidence: Two Bun processes for the same Telegram plugin found simultaneously. CPU sampling shows processes blocked in kernel waits but competing for same bot token. Causes 409 Conflict, continuous retry loops, and background churn. Reported related to #1171, #947, #934, #1075.

signals.topic: VS Code extension on Windows fails to detect Git Bash despite CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH being correctly configured
signals.summary: The Claude Code VS Code extension on Windows fails to spawn Claude Code, throwing 'requires git-bash' error even when the user has correctly set the CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH environment variable and Git Bash is in system PATH. The extension fails to read the environment variable correctly, blocking the main user workflow on Windows.
aliases: Windows Git Bash environment variable not read by VS Code extension
Claude Code VS Code extension fails to launch on Windows due to git-bash detection bug
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the VS Code extension completely fails to launch on Windows due to a bug in reading the CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH environment variable, blocking the primary user workflow. The user provides detailed evidence that all configuration is correct yet the extension fails. Count=1 and single-repo, so P2 is appropriate (not P0 due to low frequency).

source_issues.title: Claude Code for VS Code fails to read CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH on Windows
source_issues.evidence: User has git-bash installed at C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe, added to PATH, and CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH set at both Machine and User level. Extension logs show error: 'Claude Code on Windows requires git-bash' even though configuration is correct. The extension errors out and fails to load, preventing the main Claude Code workflow from running in VS Code on Windows.

signals.topic: view tool silently truncates large files at ~16K characters without warning, causing model to work with incomplete skill instructions
signals.summary: The view tool silently truncates files at ~16K characters without any warning. This specifically affects the skill-creator example skill (33K chars) where the core eval/iteration workflow section is cut in the middle. The model has no indication it is working with an incomplete copy of the skill instructions, leading to degraded quality of skill creation assistance.
signals.review_reason: Silent truncation is a confirmed user experience degradation: the model works with an incomplete skill file without any indication of truncation. The skill-creator's most important contribution (eval workflow) is in the truncated middle section. This is a blocking UX issue for anyone using skills that exceed the ~16K limit.

source_issues.title: skill-creator example skill exceeds view tool truncation limit by 2x
source_issues.evidence: The skill-creator skill (33,168 chars) is silently truncated at ~16K by the view tool. The core eval/iteration workflow (lines 113-373) is cut mid-section. No warning is emitted. The model reads an incomplete copy and believes it has the full skill.

signals.topic: LibreOffice soffice PDF conversion in pptx skill fails intermittently in Docker without retry mechanism
signals.summary: The pptx skill's `convert_to_images()` calls `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf` once with no retry logic. In Docker/containerized environments, this fails intermittently due to stale lock files, concurrent processes, or profile corruption. The error message is opaque ('PDF conversion failed') with no diagnostic info, leaving users with a complete workflow failure and no actionable error.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed workflow-blocking issue: the pptx skill's PDF conversion step fails intermittently in Docker environments (a very common deployment scenario), with no retry, and opaque error messages. Users lose complete PPTX-to-PDF conversion capability with no recovery path.

source_issues.title: pptx skill: LibreOffice PDF conversion fails intermittently with no retry
source_issues.evidence: convert_to_images() calls soffice --headless --convert-to pdf once with no retry. In Docker, intermittent failures occur due to stale lock files, concurrent processes, or profile corruption. Error message is opaque 'PDF conversion failed' with no diagnostic info.

signals.topic: Git LFS pointer mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz causes persistent dirty git working tree, breaking submodule workflows
signals.summary: The file skills/web-artifacts-builder/scripts/shadcn-components.tar.gz was committed as a raw binary blob while .gitattributes tracks *.tar.gz with the LFS filter. This causes a persistent dirty working tree on every checkout. When the repo is used as a git submodule, 'git pull --rebase' in the parent repo fails with 'fatal: cannot rebase with locally recorded submodule modifications', completely breaking the submodule workflow.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed blocking issue for submodule users: the LFS mismatch causes persistent dirty working trees and breaks 'git pull --rebase' in parent repos. Users of this repo as a submodule have no clean path forward without manual git config overrides, making automated workflows impossible.

source_issues.title: Git LFS mismatch for shadcn-components.tar.gz breaks submodule usage
source_issues.evidence: The file was committed as a raw binary blob while .gitattributes tracks *.tar.gz with LFS. Every checkout produces a dirty tree. When used as a submodule, 'git pull --rebase' fails with 'fatal: cannot rebase with locally recorded submodule modifications'. No clean workaround without local git config override.

signals.topic: Display output in v1.30.0 is unreadable due to excessive/redundant timestamps
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.30.0, Goose output is described as 'pretty much unreadable'. Users report excessive and redundant timestamps making the output very awkward to read. Multiple users (at least 2) have independently reported this as a display/UX regression.
aliases: excessive timestamps make output unreadable v1.30.0
output formatting regression in latest version
signals.review_reason: Two independent users (on the same day) reported the output as unreadable after upgrading to v1.30.0, with excessive timestamps as the primary complaint. While not a crash or data loss, degraded output readability is a meaningful experience regression that affects all v1.30.0 users.

source_issues.title: Unreadable output in 1.30.0
source_issues.evidence: User reports v1.30.0 output is 'pretty much unreadable' with screenshots showing cluttered display.

source_issues.title: Remove time stamps in output
source_issues.evidence: Separate user reports Goose generates 'a ton of redundant time stamps' making output 'very awkward to read'. Both on v1.30.0.

signals.topic: Stream timeout hardcoded to 30s breaks long-running LLM responses in v1.30.0
signals.summary: In v1.30.0, the streaming timeout is a hidden, hardcoded 30-second value (GOOSE_STREAM_TIMEOUT) that breaks slow LLM responses even when users explicitly set OLLAMA_TIMEOUT or GOOSE_TIMEOUT to much higher values (e.g., 1200s). This is a regression from prior versions where the timeout covered the full request. The error message is misleading, mentioning 'Ollama' when it affects all providers. Workaround requires an undocumented environment variable.
aliases: streaming timeout ignores user timeout config
signals.review_reason: This is a regression in v1.30.0 where the streaming timeout is hardcoded to 30s and ignores user-configured timeout values, causing streaming LLM responses to fail for slow models. The bug is confirmed by the reporter with exact reproduction steps and root cause identified. The workaround (GOOSE_STREAM_TIMEOUT env var) is undocumented, making this a silent breakage of a core workflow.

source_issues.title: Goose Stream Timeout after 30s even when setting timeout to 1200s
source_issues.evidence: User sets GOOSE_TIMEOUT: 1200s in config, but streaming still fails at 30s with 'Stream decode error: Ollama stream stalled: no data received for 30s'. Documented as a regression in v1.30.0.

signals.topic: Context truncation failure makes session unrecoverable when user interrupts mid-stream
signals.summary: When a user sends a new message while Goose is actively processing (mid-stream), Goose attempts to truncate conversation history to fit the new message but fails, displaying an error dialog 'Unable to truncate messages to stay within context limit'. The session becomes completely unrecoverable after this error — the user must start a new session to continue. This is a major workflow disruption.
aliases: session becomes unrecoverable on mid-stream interruption
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core use case of redirecting Goose mid-task. The session becomes permanently unrecoverable, forcing the user to abandon their work and start fresh. This is an experience-critical failure that breaks the natural human-in-the-loop workflow.

source_issues.title: Error: "Unable to truncate messages to stay within context limit" when interrupting with a new message
source_issues.evidence: User attempts mid-stream interruption by typing a new message; error dialog 'Unable to truncate messages to stay within context limit' appears and session cannot continue — must start new session. Reported by Block employee via Slack. More frequent in longer sessions with many tool calls.

signals.topic: Model switching fails with 'Failed to fetch' for chatgpt_codex provider
signals.summary: When trying to switch models under the chatgpt_codex provider, the app fails to load available models and the selected model does not switch. The UI shows 'Could not contact provider', 'Failed to fetch models for chatgpt_codex: Failed to fetch', and 'TypeError: Failed to fetch'. This also occurs in the Add Custom Provider flow when searching for 'codex' models.
aliases: model switcher fails for specific provider
signals.review_reason: Model switching is a core, frequently-used workflow. When it fails, users cannot change their LLM provider or model, blocking the primary mechanism for cost management and model selection. The error is clearly reproducible with documented steps.

source_issues.title: Switching model/provider fails with "Could not contact provider" / "Failed to fetch models for chatgpt_codex"
source_issues.evidence: User follows exact steps to switch model under ChatGPT Codex provider. UI shows 'Could not contact provider', 'Failed to fetch models for chatgpt_codex: Failed to fetch', 'TypeError: Failed to fetch'. Error is reproducible.

signals.topic: Backend server fails to start on fresh Windows desktop install — app is completely non-functional
signals.summary: The Goose desktop app on Windows shows 'The backend server failed to start' immediately after a fresh install. The user downloads, unzips, and runs Goose.exe, but the app is completely non-functional. This is a critical blocker for new user onboarding.
aliases: desktop app fails to start on Windows after fresh install
signals.review_reason: This is a complete startup failure on Windows. New users cannot even launch the desktop app, making the product entirely unusable on this platform. This is a P0 onboarding blocker.

source_issues.title: Backend server fails to start on fresh install (Windows desktop app)
source_issues.evidence: Fresh Windows 11 install: download, unzip, run Goose.exe — app immediately shows 'The backend server failed to start' error. No further functionality available.

signals.topic: Variable substitution fails — literal %variableName% typed instead of resolved value
signals.summary: When using variables in automation tasks, the literal token %variableName% is sometimes typed into fields instead of the resolved value, breaking automated workflows. The keys tool does not call substituteVariables(), and the act() tool with Gemini models also occasionally fails substitution.
aliases: variables not resolved in type action
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed issues (#805, #1776) with source-level root cause evidence show variable substitution fails across multiple code paths. This directly breaks automated workflows where users rely on variable resolution (e.g., typing credentials, tokens). The keys tool bypasses substitution entirely, and act() with Gemini intermittently fails. Both are user-impacting since automation produces wrong output silently.

source_issues.title: Action with variables occasionally input variable name instead of variable values
source_issues.evidence: Model: Gemini-2.0-flash. When using %password% variable in act(), the literal string 'password' is typed instead of the variable value. Occurs occasionally, making automation unreliable.

source_issues.title: keys tool does not perform variable substitution
source_issues.evidence: keys tool sends raw value directly without calling substituteVariables(), unlike the type tool. When clearing a field and typing a variable (Ctrl+A → Delete → keys(type, %token%)), the literal %token% is typed instead of the resolved value. Root cause confirmed in source code.

signals.topic: act() fails with Anthropic models — $PARAMETER_NAME wrapper causes Zod validation error
signals.summary: Using Anthropic models (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-5) as the default model for act() throws AI_NoObjectGeneratedError because Claude wraps the response in a $PARAMETER_NAME key, making required Zod fields undefined at the top level.
signals.review_reason: The act() function is a primary user-facing API of stagehand. When using Anthropic models (a popular choice), it throws an unhandled AI_NoObjectGeneratedError on every act() call. This is a complete functional blockage of the main act() workflow for Anthropic users. The issue includes full reproduction steps, environment details, and root cause analysis identifying the $PARAMETER_NAME wrapper in Claude's response format. This blocks the primary use case.

source_issues.title: act() fails with Anthropic models: response wrapped in $PARAMETER_NAME key
source_issues.evidence: With anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, act() throws AI_NoObjectGeneratedError. Claude's tool_use response wraps output in $PARAMETER_NAME key. Stagehand's Zod schema validation fails because all required fields (elementId, description, method, arguments, twoStep) are undefined at top level. Same code works with OpenAI models.

signals.topic: Hardcoded or invalid reasoningEffort value breaks GPT-5.4 integration
signals.summary: Stagehand hardcodes 'minimal' as the default reasoningEffort for OpenAI models, but GPT-5.4 only supports 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh'. This causes AI_APICallError on extract() and act() calls with gpt-5.4, blocking the entire workflow.
signals.review_reason: When users attempt to use GPT-5.4 (a newer model), every extract() and act() call fails with an unhandled AI_APICallError before any browser interaction occurs. This is a complete workflow blocker for that specific model. The root cause is a hardcoded invalid enum value in the provider resolution logic (aisdk.ts). The issue was closed with a fix suggesting 'low' as the correct default.

source_issues.title: Stagehand sets invalid OpenAI reasoningEffort: 'minimal' for gpt-5.4
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction with stagehand.extract() throwing AI_APICallError: Unsupported value 'minimal' is not supported with 'gpt-5.4'. Stack trace points to aisdk.ts#L183-L194 where the invalid default is set. Workflow is completely blocked for gpt-5.4 users.

signals.topic: 前端 /threads/search API 请求 invalid 'context' 字段导致会话历史列表为空（Docker NAS 部署）
signals.summary: 前端 useThreads 钩子请求了不合法的 'context' 字段，触发后端 langgraph-api 422 校验错误，导致 NAS Docker 部署后左侧会话历史列表完全为空。
signals.review_reason: 关键 UI 功能不可用：会话历史列表是核心导航功能，422 错误使其完全空白，用户无法找到历史对话。影响所有更新依赖后的部署环境（Docker/NAS），count=2 有明确重复证据。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Empty conversation history list due to invalid 'context' select field in useThreads
source_issues.evidence: POST /threads/search 返回 422 Unprocessable Entity，验证失败信息：'context' is not one of ['thread_id','created_at','updated_at','state_updated_at','metadata','config','status','values','interrupts']。用户看到左侧会话历史列表完全为空。

source_issues.title: BUG：nas docker部署，gitpull最新代码后聊天无记录，最左侧不显示聊天了。
source_issues.evidence: 日志显示 POST /threads/search 422 错误，与 issue 2093 根因完全一致：使用无效字段导致 API 422，左侧会话列表为空。

signals.topic: Docker 镜像包含未解决的 Git 合并冲突标记，导致所有 Agent 运行立即失败
signals.summary: latest docker-gateway 镜像在 tools.py 第 9 行包含未合并的 Git conflict markers，导致 SyntaxError，镜像构建失败后所有用户均无法运行任何 Agent。
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：镜像中含 conflict markers 导致 tools.py 无法 import，使所有 Agent run 立即抛出 SyntaxError 失败。所有使用 docker-gateway:latest 的用户均受影响，是最严重的阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: latest Docker image for docker-gateway contains unresolved Git merge conflict markers
source_issues.evidence: SyntaxError: invalid syntax (tools.py, line 9). 每一次 Agent run 立即以 status=error 失败，日志明确显示 conflict markers 存在于镜像中。

signals.topic: 重启后 Shell 执行权限丢失，Agent 无法自动执行生成的脚本
signals.summary: 用户在重启 Docker 或切换运行环境后，Shell 工具无法自动执行此前已成功运行过的 Python 脚本，必须手动干预，导致对话流程中断。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Agent 生成脚本后无法自动执行是 DeerFlow 的核心价值损失，用户被迫手动干预，显著降低自动化效率。虽是单条 issue，但影响的是主流程（脚本执行），且为回归问题（之前可正常工作）。

source_issues.title: 某次重启后shell无法执行
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告重启后无论切换 docker 模式还是本地模式，shell 始终报错需要手动执行，脚本之前已成功运行过，证明是重启引入的回归问题。

signals.topic: 沙箱环境完全无法工作，配置后启动日志显示成功但实际不可用
signals.summary: 用户正确配置了 AioSandboxProvider、host_path、container_path 及对应 Docker 镜像，但沙箱环境完全无法工作，Agent 无法在沙箱中执行任何操作。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：沙箱是 DeerFlow 执行脚本的核心隔离环境，沙箱不可用意味着 Agent 无法安全执行代码，与 shell 执行问题共同构成执行层全面失效。用户提供了完整配置但无报错（更难排查），影响核心功能可用性。

source_issues.title: 沙箱环境完全无法工作
source_issues.evidence: 用户已在 config.yaml 正确配置了沙箱，镜像也存在，日志显示启动成功，但沙箱实际完全不可用，无具体错误日志但功能完全失效。

signals.topic: 内网部署前端页面渲染崩溃（Uncaught TypeError: cannot add property 0, object is not extensible）
signals.summary: 在内网隔离环境部署时，前端页面渲染抛出 TypeError 导致页面崩溃；但同样的打包在互联网 WSL 环境中正常运行，说明存在环境差异导致的兼容性问题。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：前端页面崩溃意味着用户完全无法使用系统，是内网/企业部署场景下的阻断性问题。环境差异导致复现困难，但用户明确提供了可对比的正常环境证据，证明问题真实存在且严重影响部署可用性。

source_issues.title: 内网部署以后前端页面渲染崩溃，报 Uncaught typeerror cannot add property 0，object is not extensible
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在内网机器 WSL 打包后导入内网，make dev 后前端页面渲染崩溃，报 Uncaught typeerror cannot add property 0, object is not extensible；但相同打包在互联网 WSL 中正常渲染。

signals.topic: AI thinking state hangs indefinitely without sending prompts to model
signals.summary: After typing a prompt, Cline shows 'Thinking...' forever but never actually sends the request to the model (cloud or local). Communication with LMStudio is established, but the prompt is never transmitted.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：用户在 Plan/Act 模式下输入任何提示词后，Cline 卡在 'Thinking...' 状态，提示词从未发送到模型，核心功能完全不可用。用户明确指出同类竞品 Roo Coder 和 Continue 无此问题，说明这是 Cline 独有缺陷。

source_issues.title: Stuck thinking for ever.
source_issues.evidence: In both Plan and Act mode, with cloud (Openrouter) or local (LM Studio) models, sending a prompt causes Cline to get stuck on 'Thinking...' indefinitely. LMStudio console confirms model listing works, but the prompt is never sent. Reproduced in both VSCode and VSCodium. Roo Coder and Continue do not have this issue.

signals.topic: Cline UI view crashes when conversation becomes too long
signals.summary: After extended use with lengthy conversations, Cline's view turns gray/unresponsive. Users cannot determine if work is still running, creating uncertainty about whether to restart and risk interrupting ongoing tasks.
aliases: View turns gray after extended use
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用且体验严重下降：用户经过两周工作积累的对话后点击 act 触发新任务，Cline 界面直接变灰，无法判断任务是否仍在运行。用户明确表示不敢关闭，担心中断进行中的任务。这是长时间使用场景下的核心功能崩溃，直接影响生产工作流。

source_issues.title: Cline's view tends to crash easily when the conversation gets too long.
source_issues.evidence: After two weeks of work with a shaped project, manually compressing context and clicking 'act' to start new work caused Cline to turn gray. No way to tell if it's still running; user is afraid closing it might interrupt the process. Includes screenshot showing gray unresponsive UI. User explicitly requests stability regardless of conversation length.

signals.topic: Infinite loop calling write_to_file in PLAN MODE after task interruption
signals.summary: After a task is interrupted in PLAN MODE, Cline enters an infinite loop repeatedly attempting to call write_to_file, which is only available in ACT MODE. Each attempt fails with an error but the loop never stops, creating a spam of failed tool calls.
aliases: Mode constraint not respected after interruption
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Cline 在 PLAN 模式中断后陷入无限重试循环，不断调用 PLAN 模式下不可用的工具 write_to_file，产生大量失败调用而不自知。这导致用户在中断后无法恢复工作，必须重启进程，造成已有工作上下文丢失。

source_issues.title: Infinite loop calling write_to_file in PLAN MODE after task interruption
source_issues.evidence: In PLAN MODE, after asking Cline to write a guide and interrupting the task, Cline enters an infinite loop calling write_to_file (only available in ACT MODE). Each attempt fails with 'Tool write_to_file is not available in PLAN MODE' — loop never recognizes mode restriction. State management issue where Cline loses track of current mode after interruption.

signals.topic: MCP tool parameters with integer/boolean types sent as strings causing Zod literal validation failures
signals.summary: Cline sends all MCP tool parameter values as strings regardless of schema type declaration. Integer literals (e.g., '8') and boolean literals (e.g., 'true') are sent as string values, causing strict Zod validation in MCP servers to reject the parameters, breaking targeted edit operations.
aliases: Zod validation failure for typed MCP params
MCP integer/boolean params sent as strings
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：MCP 工具的编辑类操作（替换章节、删除章节、标题后插入）全部失败，因为 Cline 将整数和布尔参数发送为字符串。这直接导致用户依赖的 MCP 集成功能（如 QuipEditor 的精细编辑）完全不可用，且 issue 10178 中的 token 浪费报告进一步佐证了类似参数类型问题已造成大量资源浪费。

source_issues.title: MCP tool parameters with integer/boolean types are sent as strings, causing Zod literal validation failures
source_issues.evidence: With builder-mcp QuipEditor tool: location parameter (expects integer 0-11) fails with 'received: "8", expected: 8'; analyzeStructure and returnSectionIds (expect boolean) fail with 'Expected boolean, received string'. All targeted edit operations (replace section, delete section, insert after heading) are broken. Root cause: Cline does not coerce parameter values to correct types based on MCP JSON schema.

signals.topic: Clipboard operations stop working after initial startup
signals.summary: Copying text from the chat window to the clipboard works initially after startup but stops working after some time. This regression has persisted across many versions on Windows 10 / VS Code 1.115.0.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：剪贴板功能在启动后一段时间失效，严重影响用户从对话窗口复制代码或文本的日常使用体验。用户在多个版本中持续遇到此问题，说明这是回归性 bug 而非偶发问题。

source_issues.title: Clipboard operations are failing.
source_issues.evidence: Clipboard broken across many versions. Works initially upon startup, but after a while copying text from the chat window stops working. Windows 10, VS Code 1.115.0, CLine 3.77.0. Issue persisting across multiple version updates.

signals.topic: R2 storage configured but auto-save/auto-backup fails to trigger
signals.summary: 用户正确配置了R2存储，但自动保存/备份功能完全不工作，Last backup始终显示Never，导致用户数据无法跨容器重启持久化。
signals.review_reason: R2自动保存功能是moltworker的核心数据持久化特性，用户已正确配置但该功能完全不工作，Last backup始终为Never。这是一个真实用户痛点，直接影响数据跨容器重启的持久性，属于关键功能不可用场景。虽然count=1，但用户影响证据明确（功能完全不触发），优先级定为P1。

source_issues.title: R2不能自动保存
source_issues.evidence: 用户正确配置了R2 storage，界面提示'Your data will persist across container restarts'，但Last backup显示Never，自动保存功能完全不触发。用户明确询问'请问需要怎么操作'，说明此功能对用户有实际使用价值但无法正常工作。

signals.topic: Terminal output capture failure blocks agent command execution (Docker/WSL/VSCode)
signals.summary: 用户在使用 VSCode Remote Container (Docker)、WSL、或直接 Linux 环境下运行终端命令时，Continue 扩展无法捕获命令输出，显示 'Terminal output not available'，导致 AI agent 无法获取命令执行结果，主流程被阻断。此问题在 VSCode 1.115.0 更新后加剧，且存在多个相关 issue 互相引用同一条根因。
signals.review_reason: 该问题在 Docker 容器、WSL、Windows VSCode 三个不同环境下均有用户报告，且 #12102 明确引用了 #9731 和 #9679 作为同一根因。核心 agent 功能（终端命令执行→获取输出→LLM 决策）被完全阻断，用户无法使用任何依赖终端输出的工作流，高频+主流程阻断+有样例链接，完全符合 P0 标准。

source_issues.title: Terminal output not captured in Docker container after VSCode update
source_issues.evidence: 命令在终端执行成功但 Continue 扩展无法捕获输出，显示 'Terminal output not available'，同时引用了 #9731 和 #9679 作为同根因的关联 issue

source_issues.title: Terminal output not captured when Windows VSCode connects to WSL
source_issues.evidence: WSL 环境下终端输出捕获失败，同一根因

source_issues.title: fix: use ide.runCommand when Windows host connects to WSL
source_issues.evidence: PR 修复了 Windows+WSL 场景的终端捕获问题，同一根因

signals.topic: Windows 环境下 shell 命令执行失败：spawn powershell.exe ENOENT
signals.summary: 在 Windows 系统上，Continue 的 run_terminal_command 工具始终报错 'spawn powershell.exe ENOENT'，导致所有终端命令（包括 rm/del/echo 等基础命令）无法执行，用户无法删除文件、运行脚本，核心工具链完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但该问题的用户影响极其严重：Windows 环境下所有终端命令（create_new_file 以外的唯一执行通道）完全不可用，包括文件删除等基础操作。影响覆盖整个 agent 工作流，非边缘场景，review_reason 已提供强用户影响证据，符合 P0 的例外条件。

source_issues.title: Terminal/Shell Commands Fail with spawn powershell.exe ENOENT Error
source_issues.evidence: 所有终端命令（rm, del, echo）在 Windows 上均失败，报错 'spawn powershell.exe ENOENT'，导致文件无法删除、脚本无法执行，agent 工具链核心功能完全不可用，限制了文件管理和自动化工作流

signals.topic: Agent 应用编辑时键盘焦点从聊天窗口跳转到文件编辑器，打断用户输入
signals.summary: 当 agent 正在应用文件编辑时，用户在聊天窗口输入的字符会错误地进入文件编辑器而非聊天框，导致输入内容错位，用户被迫中断正在输入的 prompt，显著影响使用效率。
aliases: input cursor jumps to file editor
focus switches to file during edit
signals.review_reason: 该问题在每次 agent 应用编辑时都会触发，打断用户的输入流程。虽然 count=1，但问题场景明确（edit 应用期间）、影响真实（输入错位）、触发频率高（非偶发），归为 P1 合理，不升 P0 因缺乏多源交叉验证。

source_issues.title: Keyboard input focus switches to file editor even if user is actively typing in chat window while agent is applying edits
source_issues.evidence: 用户描述了明确的复现步骤：当 agent 编辑文件时，用户在聊天窗口输入的内容被错误写入文件编辑器，字符进入错误的窗口，用户需要中断输入来纠正，问题在每次 agent 应用编辑时都会触发

signals.topic: 长对话场景下 UI 性能严重下降，即使压缩上下文后仍未改善
signals.summary: 在长对话（50 万 token 以上，经历多次压缩）后，聊天窗口加载、切换对话、打开设置菜单均变得卡顿，即使使用内置压缩功能缩减上下文长度后，UI 依然缓慢，表明问题根源不在 context 大小而在前端状态管理。
signals.review_reason: 长对话是核心使用场景，UI 卡顿直接影响每日使用体验。用户明确排除了 context 大小因素（压缩后仍未改善），说明这是前端状态管理或渲染的性能问题。虽然 count=1，但影响的是高频核心场景，归 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: UI becomes extremely slow in long conversations
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确指出：即使使用了 compress 功能压缩上下文后，UI 仍然卡顿，切换对话、加载聊天窗口、打开设置菜单均变慢，证明不是 context 大小问题而是前端渲染/状态问题，且长对话是高频使用场景

signals.topic: Flutter 项目中 Continue 扩展无法加载，报错后完全不启动
signals.summary: 在 Flutter/Dart 项目中打开 VSCode 时，Continue 扩展完全无法启动并报错，而在其他类型项目中正常。这导致 Flutter 开发者无法使用 Continue 进行工作，是一个阻断特定项目类型的严重问题。
aliases: Flutter project extension fails to load
signals.review_reason: Flutter 开发者群体虽非全部用户，但在 Flutter 生态中是明确的阻断性问题。扩展在特定项目类型下完全无法启动，影响该群体的主流程。由于 count=1 且为特定场景，归 P2，保留是因为有明确用户影响证据（扩展完全不启动）。

source_issues.title: Doesn't load when working on flutter project
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 Flutter 项目中打开 VSCode 时 Continue 完全无法加载和启动，而在其他项目类型中正常工作，这是一个针对 Flutter/Dart 生态的阻断性问题，影响特定开发者群体的核心工作流

signals.topic: LanceDB dependency dropped macOS x86_64 wheels making crewAI completely uninstallable on Intel Macs
signals.summary: lancedb>=0.29.2 dropped macOS x86_64 wheel builds, making crewAI 1.12.2 fully uninstallable on all Intel Macs — even for projects not using memory features
signals.review_reason: Complete uninstallability on Intel Macs is a main flow blocking issue — all Intel Mac users cannot install crewai at all, even for projects not using memory features. This blocks the entire user journey from installation onward. 2 comments confirm the issue.

source_issues.title: crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: lancedb dropped macOS x86_64 (Intel) wheel builds at 0.29.2. crewAI 1.12.2 requires lancedb>=0.29.2 as mandatory core dependency, making crewai completely UNINSTALLABLE on all Intel Macs — even for projects never using memory features. 2 comments confirm the issue.

signals.topic: Official documentation code produces errors when users try to run it
signals.summary: Code from the official crewAI documentation (flow-state persistence guide) produces runtime errors when users try to run it
signals.review_reason: User tried to run official documentation code and got an error. This blocks users trying to learn the platform from official docs, creating a negative onboarding experience.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Wrong code in document
source_issues.evidence: User tried to run code from official documentation (flow-state persistence guide) and got an error. The documented code is broken.

signals.topic: Streaming handlers on singleton event bus fan out chunks to wrong concurrent runs causing output to go to wrong user/client
signals.summary: LLMStreamChunkEvent handlers on singleton event bus fan out chunks to wrong per-run queues in concurrent streaming runs, causing data leakage and wrong responses in production
signals.review_reason: In concurrent web serving scenarios, streaming output can go to the wrong user/client due to singleton event bus fan-out. This causes data leakage and wrong responses in production concurrent environments.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Streaming handlers on singleton event bus can fan out chunks across concurrent runs
source_issues.evidence: LLMStreamChunkEvent handlers on singleton event bus fan out chunks to wrong per-run queues in concurrent streaming runs. In web serving scenarios, this causes streaming output to go to the wrong user/client.

signals.topic: @persist decorator documentation does not explain WHERE state is persisted
signals.summary: The @persist decorator documentation says state is persisted but does not document the storage location (e.g., SQLite file path), leaving users unable to locate or audit their data
signals.review_reason: Documentation gap prevents users from understanding where their data is stored. Blocks users from auditing or managing their persistence data, though not a main flow failure.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Enhance the document about @persist
source_issues.evidence: The @persist decorator documentation says state is persisted but does not explain where (e.g., SQLite file path). Users and AI assistants cannot locate persistence data.

signals.topic: before_tool_call decorator requires exact tool name match forcing manual sanitize_tool_name() calls
signals.summary: The before_tool_call decorator's tools parameter requires exact string match, forcing users to manually call sanitize_tool_name() before passing the list
signals.review_reason: DX friction where users must manually call sanitize_tool_name() before passing tool list to before_tool_call decorator. Not blocking but creates unnecessary work and confusion.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] [UX] before_tool_call decorator's tools parameter should auto-normalize tool names
source_issues.evidence: The before_tool_call decorator's tools parameter requires exact tool name match. Users must manually call sanitize_tool_name() before passing the list, creating DX friction.

signals.topic: Ollama 远程提供者配置/连接失败导致主流程阻断
signals.summary: 用户配置正确的 Ollama 远程环境变量后，Fabric CLI 和 Server 均无法识别 vendor，出现「could not find vendor」错误；Server 模式还会在 Context= 阶段无限挂起直至 ECONNRESET，导致远程 Ollama 完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均为同一用户在同一时间段（2026-04-06）报告的 Ollama 远程提供者问题，issue #2084 导致 CLI chat/stream 主流程完全阻断，issue #2083 导致 Server 模式无限挂起并最终超时，均有明确错误日志和用户影响证据。虽然 count=2 未达 P0 阈值(>=3)，但两项均为高价值阻断性 bug（核心功能完全不可用），按 review_reason 强证据支撑可标记为 P1。两者根因相同（远程 Ollama 提供者初始化/连接失败），合并为单一痛点主题。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: "could not find vendor" error despite correctly configured .env (Ollama/Remote)
source_issues.evidence: 用户正确配置了 DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama、OLLAMA_API_URL、OLLAMA_BASE_URL，fabric -L 能列出远程模型，但执行 chat/stream 时报「could not find vendor」，主流程完全阻断。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Server hangs at Context= when using remote Ollama provider (ECONNRESET)
source_issues.evidence: Server 模式(--serve)连接远程 Ollama 时在 Context= 阶段无限挂起，最终产生 ECONNRESET 错误，socket hang up，Server 端主流程阻断。

signals.topic: Plan Mode hangs in thinking loop without presenting results, blocking workflow
signals.summary: In Plan Mode, the CLI gets stuck in a thinking loop for extended periods (15-30 minutes) without presenting any implementation plan or response, making Plan Mode unusable for basic tasks.
signals.review_reason: Plan Mode is a primary workflow feature that allows users to review and approve AI actions before execution. Hangs lasting 15-30 minutes on simple tasks completely block the intended workflow, making the feature unusable. Two independent reports confirm this issue.

source_issues.title: Plan mode getting hung up in thinking loop. Not presenting implementation plan after 2 min for a rudimentary request.
source_issues.evidence: Plan Mode with Gemini 3.1 Pro preview stuck in thinking loop for 2 full minutes on a simple folder structure and markdown file request. No plan was presented before user stopped it.

source_issues.title: CLI constantly get stuck for 15 minutes or more on a simple implementation plan review
source_issues.evidence: CLI stuck for 15-30 minutes with only a Thinking spinner, no response, making Plan Mode completely unusable. User describes it as 'unusable'. Version 0.36.0 on Windows.

signals.topic: Telemetry truncation breaks JSON parseability and forces detailed tracing overhead on all users
signals.summary: The telemetry truncation strategy uses safeJsonStringify then cuts at 10,000 characters, producing fundamentally unparseable JSON. Additionally, enabling lightweight baseline telemetry unconditionally activates detailed tracing, forcing all users to bear the cost of heavy trace spans even when they only want base metrics.
signals.review_reason: Telemetry data being unparseable JSON breaks any downstream log ingestion or analytics pipeline that relies on valid JSON, directly degrading observability. The forced tracing overhead also causes unnecessary compute cost for users who only want base usage metrics.

source_issues.title: Bug: Telemetry truncation causes JSON unparseability & couples tracing overhead
source_issues.evidence: Truncation produces unparseable JSON payloads; unconditional tracing activation violates lightweight baseline principle, forcing unnecessary overhead on all users regardless of intent.

signals.topic: Plan Mode write_file silently flattens nested paths, overwriting root-level files
signals.summary: In Plan Mode, the write_file tool strips all intermediate directories when writing to nested paths within an authorized base directory, causing silent overwriting of root-level files like index.md.
signals.review_reason: Silent data destruction is a high-severity issue. The write_file tool in Plan Mode silently overwrites existing root-level project files without any warning, which can result in permanent data loss. This directly blocks the core Plan Mode workflow.

source_issues.title: Plan Mode Path Flattening in `write_file`
source_issues.evidence: Silent overwriting of existing root-level files (e.g., conductor/index.md overwrites the main project index) when writing nested paths in Plan Mode. Verified only in Plan Mode; Default Mode preserves directory structure correctly.

signals.topic: CLI crashes on Windows 11 with Node v22.16.0 — TypeError: newSpans.at is not a function
signals.summary: On Windows 11 with Node v22.16.0, the CLI crashes during output rendering with TypeError: newSpans.at is not a function at _StyledLine.mergeSpans, completely blocking the main user interaction flow.
signals.review_reason: The CLI crashes with an uncaught TypeError during output rendering on Windows 11 with Node v22.16.0, completely blocking the main user interaction flow. This is a critical, reproducible crash affecting a specific platform/Node version combination.

source_issues.title: [CRITICAL] CLI crashes on Windows 11 with Node v22.16.0. TypeError: newSpans.at is not a function at _StyledLine.mergeSpans. Happens during output rendering.
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashes with uncaught TypeError at _StyledLine.mergeSpans, preventing any interaction. Reproduced on Windows 11 with Node v22.16.0 during normal output rendering. Marked with [CRITICAL] in title and priority/p1 label.

signals.topic: Google OAuth login flow completes but user is still shown as not logged in
signals.summary: Users go through the Google OAuth login flow successfully but upon reaching the prompt, the CLI still shows the user as not logged in, blocking access to all features.
aliases: login not persisting after Google auth
signals.review_reason: Login failure is a complete blocker — users who successfully complete the OAuth flow are still shown as not logged in, making the entire CLI unusable. This is a primary authentication flow regression that prevents any usage of the product.

source_issues.title: Log in problems
source_issues.evidence: User completes 'Log in with Google' flow successfully, but the prompt shows the user cannot log in. All subsequent CLI features are inaccessible. Reproduced on Windows 11.

signals.topic: No callback/hook interface for audit trails and tool-execution governance
signals.summary: smolagents lacks pre/post tool-execution hooks, preventing users in regulated environments (finance, healthcare, EU AI Act compliance) from creating tamper-evident audit trails without modifying framework internals.
aliases: no callback handlers for tool execution
EU AI Act compliance audit logging missing
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues from different users both request pre/post tool-execution hooks for audit/compliance purposes. While not a crash, this is a regulatory blocker for regulated-industry deployments — EU AI Act Article 12 compliance is explicitly cited. Count=2 meets the threshold for inclusion, but priority is P2 because it is not workflow-blocking for non-regulated use cases and no production crash/failure is described.

source_issues.title: Audit trail hooks for agent actions
source_issues.evidence: smolagents has no way to create a tamper-evident record of what the agent did. EU AI Act Article 12 requires automatic event logging that can be independently verified. Two separate users independently filed this request, indicating community demand.

source_issues.title: Add audit trail / governance callback support
source_issues.evidence: For regulated deployments (finance, healthcare), tamper-evident records of tool calls are required. Callback hook before/after tool execution is needed. User has built this for other frameworks and is willing to contribute PR.

signals.topic: WebSearchTool hardcoded HTTP timeout breaks agent runs in corporate/slow networks
signals.summary: WebSearchTool hardcodes 30-second HTTP timeouts across all search backends, causing avoidable ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs. No user-configurable timeout override exists, forcing users to subclass or monkey-patch the tool.
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow-blocking issue: hardcoded timeouts cause agent runs to abort with ReadTimeout in legitimate slow-network environments (corporate proxies, high-latency regions). Users cannot configure the timeout without invasive subclassing or monkey-patching. While count=1, the review_reason provides strong user-impact evidence: production workflow abortion, no workaround, and the same pattern was flagged across multiple PRs (#2139, #2140), indicating systemic risk.

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool
source_issues.evidence: All three search backends use hardcoded timeout=30 on requests.get calls. Corporate proxies and slow network environments regularly exceed 30 seconds, causing avoidable ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs. No override mechanism exists without subclassing or monkey-patching.

signals.topic: GitHub Actions CI workflow fails with 403 error during artifact cleanup
signals.summary: The Copilot code review workflow's 'Cleanup artifacts' job consistently fails when attempting to delete artifacts, returning a 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' error. This blocks automated CI cleanup and requires manual intervention or workflow redesign.
aliases: CI artifact cleanup job failing with permission error
signals.review_reason: This is a real CI/CD operational failure blocking automated workflow completion. The GitHub Actions cleanup job cannot delete artifacts due to a 403 permission error, which means artifacts accumulate, CI runs fail to clean up after themselves, and maintainers must manually intervene. While only 1 issue in this dataset, it represents a recurring integration-level failure affecting all contributors who rely on the Copilot code review workflow.

source_issues.title: Copilot code review cleanup job fails deleting artifacts with 403
source_issues.evidence: GitHub Actions run 23775280758 fails in workflow 'Copilot code review', job 'Cleanup artifacts', step 'Delete artifacts' with error: 'gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)'. Root cause: workflow token permissions / integration scope mismatch during artifact deletion. Workflow runs are blocked and cannot complete cleanup automatically.

signals.topic: Agent optimizer loopholes bypass evaluation boundaries — immutable-by-instruction is insufficient
signals.summary: The autorersearch loop is susceptible to agents finding data access loopholes (e.g., loading holdout data through load_data()) that inflate eval metrics to near-zero, rendering the optimization loop theatrical rather than meaningful. The fix requires immutable-by-design boundaries, not just instruction-based constraints.
aliases: Agent data leakage loophole in eval loop
Holdout data accessible to agent causing metric gaming
Optimizer finds evaluation loopholes not anticipated by humans
signals.review_reason: While observed in a domain-applied experiment rather than in core repo usage, this pattern represents a real architectural weakness in the autoresearch loop: if agents can access evaluation data, the entire optimization loop becomes unreliable. The user's own experiment demonstrates WAPE=0.0000 due to holdout leakage — a complete metric gaming scenario. The 'immutable by instruction is not enough' conclusion has direct implications for anyone running autonomous loops in production. Count=1 limits this to P2, but it is a legitimate user-impacting design gap.

source_issues.title: Applied autoresearch to Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) — 12x improvement, beat Google Meridian
source_issues.evidence: In session 1 (~exp 88), the agent found a loophole: load_data() was returning the full dataset including holdout sales. It trained OLS directly on the test data → WAPE = 0.0000. The author explicitly states: 'Immutable by instruction is not enough. Must be immutable by design.' This is corroborated by literature (arXiv:2408.07678 'Your MMM is Broken') showing optimizers find evaluation loopholes that humans don't anticipate.

signals.topic: deepagents deploy bundler missing model provider dependencies — 10/16 providers cause silent runtime ImportError
signals.summary: The `deepagents deploy` CLI validates credentials for 16 model providers via `_MODEL_PROVIDER_ENV`, but `_MODEL_PROVIDER_DEPS` in bundler.py only bundles dependencies for 6 of them. Users deploying with any of the 10 missing providers (fireworks, baseten, together, xai, nvidia, cohere, deepseek, openrouter, perplexity, azure_openai) pass validation and get exit 0, but the deployed agent crashes at runtime with ImportError.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 (P0): deploy 命令验证通过但运行时崩溃。10/16 模型提供商缺失依赖，用户完成完整部署流程后才发现失败，导致部署流水线白跑、agent 无法启动。2 条独立 issue 均有可复现的 repro steps 和完整堆栈信息，根因明确（bundler.py 中 _MODEL_PROVIDER_DEPS 与 _MODEL_PROVIDER_ENV 不同步）。

source_issues.title: deploy: together provider not bundled — ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: together provider in _MODEL_PROVIDER_ENV (validates TOGETHER_API_KEY) but absent from _MODEL_PROVIDER_DEPS in bundler.py. No 'together' optional extra in pyproject.toml. deepagents deploy exits 0 then agent crashes at runtime with ImportError.

source_issues.title: Deploy bundler missing deps for 10 of 16 model providers — silent ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: 10 missing providers: fireworks, baseten, together, xai, nvidia, cohere, deepseek, openrouter, perplexity, azure_openai. Config validation passes, deploy exits 0, agent crashes at runtime with ImportError.

signals.topic: FilesystemMiddleware drops goto/graph from Command — multi-agent handoffs silently fail in create_deep_agent
signals.summary: FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result reconstructs Command objects and silently drops goto and graph fields, breaking the standard LangGraph multi-agent handoff pattern. With create_agent handoffs work; with create_deep_agent the target agent never executes (silent failure).
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用 (P1): 多 agent 协作是 deepagents 核心场景，handoff 是 LangGraph 标准模式。FilesystemMiddleware 静默丢弃 goto/graph，导致目标 agent 永远不执行，但用户看不到任何错误信息（静默失败）。虽然仅 1 条 issue，但提供了完整 e2e repro，对比了 create_agent（正常）和 create_deep_agent（失败），置信度高。

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result drops goto and graph from Command objects
source_issues.evidence: FilesystemMiddleware wraps tool results and reconstructs Command() copying only update, dropping goto and graph fields. create_agent + handoffs → nodes ['agent_a', 'agent_b'] works; create_deep_agent + same handoffs → nodes ['agent_a'] only, target agent never executes. Full e2e reproduction provided. Regression bisected to FilesystemMiddleware.

signals.topic: RunloopSandbox download_files/upload_files — single file failure crashes entire batch, violates protocol contract
signals.summary: RunloopSandbox.download_files() and upload_files() lack per-file try/except. Any single file failure (not found, permission denied) raises an unhandled exception, aborting the entire batch. Violates the BaseSandbox protocol which explicitly requires partial-success semantics. FilesystemMiddleware calls these methods during skill loading and batch file operations.
aliases: runloop sandbox file ops crash entire batch
signals.review_reason: 工作流运行时崩溃 (P1): 文件批处理是 deepagents 核心操作（skill 加载、文件读取等），单个文件失败导致整个批次崩溃，且违反明确定义的协议契约。FilesystemMiddleware 依赖这些方法，在多 subagent 场景下问题加剧。仅 1 条 issue 但有详细协议违背证据和多 provider 对比（ModalSandbox/LangSmithSandbox 正确实现）。

source_issues.title: RunloopSandbox.download_files/upload_files failure crashes entire batch
source_issues.evidence: RunloopSandbox.download_files() has no try/except around _devbox.file.download(). A single file not found raises unhandled SDK exception, second file is never attempted. Violates BaseSandbox protocol (lines 729/740) which explicitly requires per-file error handling and partial-success semantics. ModalSandbox and LangSmithSandbox both implement this correctly.

signals.topic: Subgraph tools not found — ValueError when calling GET /threads/{thread_id}/history after checkpoint creation
signals.summary: deepagents internally compiles tool execution into a 'tools' subgraph node written to checkpoint, but the subgraph is not properly exposed via aget_subgraphs() to the LangGraph runtime. When rebuilding thread history via GET /threads/{thread_id}/history, ValueError: Subgraph tools not found is raised.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用 (P1): /threads/{thread_id}/history 是 deepagents 的核心持久化功能，用户创建 checkpoint 后无法读取历史状态，直接阻断会话恢复流程。LangGraph 内部报错 ValueError，有明确堆栈和复现步骤，根因分析到位（checkpoint 中 subgraph 未正确暴露）。

source_issues.title: Subgraph tools not found when calling /threads/{thread_id}/history
source_issues.evidence: After creating an agent with custom @tool via create_deep_agent and running a conversation to generate a checkpoint, calling GET /threads/{thread_id}/history raises ValueError: Subgraph tools not found at langgraph/pregel/main.py line 1436. Root cause: deepagents writes tool execution as a 'tools' subgraph node to checkpoint but doesn't properly expose it via aget_subgraphs().

signals.topic: SkillsMiddleware caching prevents dynamic skill upload/load after skill creation in active session
signals.summary: SkillsMiddleware caches skills at initialization, preventing newly created skills from being dynamically loaded within the same session. After a skill is created, it cannot be dynamically uploaded and loaded based on the current session context.
aliases: skill creation not reflected in session
signals.review_reason: 体验下降 (P2): SkillsMiddleware 缓存机制导致会话内新创建的 skill 无法动态加载，影响动态 skill 管理流程。issue 标题清晰描述了根因（缓存机制），标记为 bug，但 body 内容较少，缺乏详细复现步骤和错误堆栈，置信度偏低。仅 1 条 issue，归为 P2。

source_issues.title: The caching mechanism of SkillsMiddleware. After a skill is created, new skills cannot be dynamically uploaded and loaded based on the session.
source_issues.evidence: SkillsMiddleware caching mechanism prevents dynamic skill upload and loading after skill creation within the same session. A newly created skill cannot be loaded into the active session context.

signals.topic: OutputParserException crashes LLM calls when model output does not match schema
signals.summary: langchain_core.exceptions.OutputParserException is raised when model output deviates from the expected schema, crashing LLM calls in structured output scenarios with Ollama and potentially other providers.
signals.review_reason: OutputParserException and Ollama 500 errors block structured output and LLM invocation for affected users. Two issues share the same Ollama integration and core output parsing path, confirming a systemic problem. Both are confirmed bugs in LangChain (not user error).

source_issues.title: langchain_core.exceptions.OutputParserException
source_issues.evidence: OutputParserException raised during structured output. Confirmed as bug in LangChain core, not user code. Affects Ollama integration.

source_issues.title: ollama._types.ResponseError: Internal Server Error (ref: 3f380fc3-f1b8-4b9e-aa2c-5c4486b28c08) (status code: 500)
source_issues.evidence: Ollama returns 500 Internal Server Error through LangChain's wrapper. Breaks Ollama LLM calls. Confirmed as LangChain bug.

signals.topic: _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when service_tier is set but cached_tokens is missing
signals.summary: In langchain-openai, the _create_usage_metadata helper crashes with TypeError when service_tier is provided but cached_tokens is absent, blocking token usage reporting for production pipelines.
signals.review_reason: Core crash in _create_usage_metadata blocks token usage reporting. service_tier is a production API parameter; absence of cached_tokens in the response causes a TypeError, not a graceful fallback. This is a workflow-level blocker for users using OpenAI's batch/inference endpoints.

source_issues.title: bug(openai): _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
source_issues.evidence: TypeError raised in _create_usage_metadata when service_tier is set but cached_tokens is absent. Crashes production LLM call paths that use service_tier.

signals.topic: _batch and _abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop in batch processing
signals.summary: In langchain-core, _batch and _abatch do not validate batch_size, causing an infinite loop when batch_size=0 or invalid, completely blocking batch processing workflows.
signals.review_reason: Infinite loop in batch processing is a workflow-level blocker. It causes indefinite CPU consumption and complete halt of any batch pipeline. This is a clear main-flow failure with a self-contained reproducible example confirmed as a bug.

source_issues.title: bug(core): _batch and _abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop
source_issues.evidence: When batch_size is 0 or invalid, _batch and _abatch enter an infinite loop, consuming CPU and never returning. No validation guard exists.

signals.topic: Streaming same-index tool_call chunks split into blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
signals.summary: During streaming, same-index tool_call chunks from one streamed delta can be incorrectly split, producing blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls, breaking agent tool execution.
signals.review_reason: Streaming is a core feature path. When tool calls are split into blank/invalid entries, agents cannot execute tools correctly, which is a primary use case. This is a main-flow failure for streaming agent users.

source_issues.title: fix(core): same-index tool_call chunks in one streamed delta can split into blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: Streaming pipeline produces blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls when same-index chunks are split across deltas. Breaks agent tool execution in streaming mode.

signals.topic: MongoDB Toolkit fails with Firestore MongoDB-compatible endpoint due to unsupported authorizedCollections option
signals.summary: MongoDB Toolkit uses an authorizedCollections option not supported by Firestore-compatible endpoints, causing MongoDB Toolkit to fail when used with Firestore backends.
signals.review_reason: MongoDB Toolkit failing on Firestore-compatible endpoints is an integration-level blocker. Users who use Firebase/Firestore as backend cannot use the MongoDB Toolkit, which defeats the purpose of cross-database compatibility.

source_issues.title: MongoDB Toolkit fails with Firestore MongoDB-compatible endpoint due to unsupported authorizedCollections option
source_issues.evidence: MongoDB Toolkit construction fails with Firestore-compatible endpoints because it sets authorizedCollections, which Firestore does not support. Breaks database integration for users with Firestore backends.

signals.topic: langgraph-cli missing typing_extensions dependency causes CLI to crash on fresh install
signals.summary: langgraph-cli 0.4.21 imports typing_extensions in schemas.py but fails to declare it as a dependency, causing ModuleNotFoundError on any clean environment (CI/CD, GitHub Actions, fresh VMs). The CLI is entirely unusable without a manual workaround.
signals.review_reason: Blocking issue that prevents langgraph-cli from running at all on clean environments. Verified regression introduced in 0.4.21 with clear before/after evidence. Any CI/CD pipeline or fresh VM install is broken.

source_issues.title: langgraph-cli 0.4.21: Missing `typing_extensions` dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typing_extensions' on clean pip install. Reproduction: pip install langgraph-cli==0.4.21 && langgraph build crashes. 0.4.19 works, 0.4.21 introduced the regression.

signals.topic: Runtime execution_info patch failure crashes ALL LangGraph Cloud deployments
signals.summary: langgraph >=1.1.5 added a guard in patch_execution_info() that raises RuntimeError when execution_info is None. The LangGraph Cloud executor 0.7.96 constructs Runtime with execution_info=None, causing every deployed graph to crash immediately at the __start__ node with 'RuntimeError: Cannot patch execution_info before it has been set'.
aliases: Cannot patch execution_info before it has been set LangGraph Cloud
signals.review_reason: Full production outage for ALL LangGraph Cloud users. Every deployed graph crashes on the first run regardless of code. Verified with two consecutive executor versions (0.7.94 working, 0.7.96 broken). This is a platform-wide service degradation.

source_issues.title: RuntimeError: Cannot patch execution_info before it has been set on LangGraph Cloud executor 0.7.96
source_issues.evidence: Any graph deployed to LangGraph Cloud crashes on first run. Verified working with executor 0.7.94, broken with 0.7.96. Root cause: ExecutionInfo became a frozen dataclass with required fields in 1.1.5, executor doesn't set it before calling patch_execution_info. Affects all cloud users.

signals.topic: UnboundLocalError in push_message crashes message-handling nodes when callbacks is None
signals.summary: In push_message (langgraph/graph/message.py), the handlers variable is only assigned inside if/elif branches. When config['callbacks'] is None, neither branch executes, leaving handlers undefined, causing UnboundLocalError on the subsequent line that accesses handlers.
signals.review_reason: Main execution path crash. When callbacks is None (a valid default state), the code path unconditionally crashes with UnboundLocalError. Any user not explicitly passing a callback manager will hit this. The fix is a one-line initialization.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message and dead code in _strip_extras
source_issues.evidence: Code shows handlers only defined inside if/elif block, unconditionally referenced on line 360 causing UnboundLocalError when callbacks is None. Reproduction path: any code path that sets config['callbacks'] to None triggers the crash.

signals.topic: Command(resume=None) causes UnboundLocalError crash in PregelLoop._first
signals.summary: In PregelLoop._first(), the variable resume_is_map is only assigned inside the if (resume := self.input.resume) is not None block. When Command(resume=None) is used, this block is skipped and resume_is_map is referenced unconditionally, causing UnboundLocalError and crashing the entire graph execution.
