signals.review_reason: Main workflow execution crash. The interrupt-and-resume pattern is a core LangGraph feature. Passing resume=None (which is a common default scenario) crashes the entire graph loop with an unrelated UnboundLocalError instead of the expected EmptyInputError.

source_issues.title: UnboundLocalError: resume_is_map when using Command(resume=None)
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing UnboundLocalError at _loop.py:663 in _first(). Minimal reproduction: compile graph with checkpointer, invoke with interrupt, resume with Command(resume=None). Should raise EmptyInputError but crashes with UnboundLocalError instead.

signals.topic: langgraph-prebuilt 1.0.9 breaks with older langgraph versions — ImportError on ServerInfo
signals.summary: langgraph-prebuilt 1.0.9 introduced a new import: 'from langgraph.runtime import ExecutionInfo, ServerInfo'. This breaks any project pinned to langgraph <1.1.5 (e.g. langgraph==1.1.3), causing ImportError on import. Users cannot upgrade prebuilt without also upgrading the core library.
signals.review_reason: Breaking change affecting all users with pinned older langgraph versions. While the core library eventually needs upgrade, the semver range in pyproject.toml is misleading. Users encounter a confusing ImportError instead of a clear version mismatch message. Count=1 because it's a single version-specific breaking change.

source_issues.title: `langgraph-prebuilt` v1.0.9 breaks with older versions of `langgraph`. Cannot import name 'ServerInfo' from 'langgraph.runtime'
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible on any project pinning langgraph<1.1.5: 'from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode' raises ImportError. pyproject.toml references a langgraph>=1.1.0 requirement that doesn't capture this breaking change. 8 comments indicating widespread user impact.

signals.topic: SQLAlchemy DetachedInstanceError blocks password reset and plugin settings API
signals.summary: 用户登录后访问插件设置或发起密码重置时，DB session 已关闭导致 DetachedInstanceError，API 返回 500。影响核心登录和账户管理流程。
signals.review_reason: 3 条独立 issue 均指向同一根本原因：get_account_by_email_with_case_fallback / TenantPluginPermission 在 session 关闭后被访问。直接阻断登录后访问插件设置和密码重置两个核心流程。count=3 且涉及主流程阻断，满足 P0 标准。

source_issues.title: sqlalchemy.orm.exc.DetachedInstanceError
source_issues.evidence: 访问 /console/api/workspaces/current/plugin/preferences/fetch 时抛出 DetachedInstanceError，API 返回 500。调用链：plugin.py:778 访问 permission.install_permission 属性时 session 已关闭。

source_issues.title: get_account_by_email_with_case_fallback lead account detach instance error
source_issues.evidence: 密码重置流程中 get_account_by_email_with_case_fallback 返回的 Account 对象在 session 关闭后被访问，导致 DetachedInstanceError，密码重置功能完全不可用。

source_issues.title: how to avoid session closed then visit
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确报告经常遇到此问题，讨论中有多人参与，描述与 #34907/#34902 相同的根本原因：get_account_by_email_with_case_fallback 在 session 关闭后被访问。

signals.topic: Chatflow 多轮对话预览中文件上传随机失败（Cloud）
signals.summary: Chatflow 多轮对话预览中，特定文件（8.13KB txt）在后续轮次上传失败，反复重试无效，阻断预览工作流。
aliases: file upload fails chatflow preview cloud
signals.review_reason: 明确的主流程阻断：多轮 Chatflow 预览是核心使用场景，文件上传是基础功能，付费用户反复失败且无可靠解决方案。虽然 count=1，但影响付费用户核心工作流，review_reason 给出强证据，定 P1。

source_issues.title: File upload fails in Chatflow preview on Cloud (Professional plan)
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 Professional 付费计划 ($59/月) 下，多轮 Chatflow 预览中上传 .txt 文件（8.13KB，远低于 15MB 限制）时持续报错「ファイルのアップロードに失敗しました」，无法通过刷新浏览器解决（会丢失对话记忆）。用户明确表示「blocks our workflow」且「need a fundamental fix, not a temporary workaround」。

signals.topic: Python Sandbox 代码执行中文件系统操作失败（FileNotFoundError）
signals.summary: Python 代码节点尝试在沙盒中创建目录或文件时抛出 FileNotFoundError，目录创建操作失败，导致依赖文件输出的工作流完全不可用。
aliases: python code execution sandbox file not found
signals.review_reason: Sandbox 文件系统操作失败导致代码执行节点无法完成，阻断工作流。虽然 count=1，但路径明确（/var/sandbox/sandbox-python/tmp），是代码节点的核心场景，定 P1。

source_issues.title: I want to create a /app/ directory using the workflow of dify. I'm using Python code execution for this, but I'm encountering an error.
source_issues.evidence: Python 代码节点执行时尝试 os.makedirs('/var/sandbox/sandbox-python/tmp') 失败，抛出 FileNotFoundError。目录创建是工作流中常见需求，此错误导致所有依赖文件输出的代码节点工作流完全失败。

signals.topic: Chatflow 流式输出中并行 Iteration 节点阻塞其他分支节点
signals.summary: Chatflow 配置并行 Iteration 节点时，其下游的 Answer/Code 节点被错误地阻塞到 Iteration 完成后才执行，导致流式输出无法提前返回，用户需等待 120 秒而非预期的 10 秒。
aliases: parallel iteration node blocks downstream nodes
signals.review_reason: 并行执行设计存在根本性缺陷：并行 Iteration 反而阻塞其他分支的流式输出，导致 10 秒响应被延迟到 120 秒。严重影响 Chatflow 流式输出的核心价值。虽然 count=1，但用户提供了详细测试证据和截图，P1 合理。

source_issues.title: Chatflow: Parallel iteration node blocks downstream nodes in other concurrent branches
source_issues.evidence: 并行模式 Iteration 节点（120秒任务）与上游分支（10秒）并行执行时，下游 Answer 节点被错误阻塞直到 Iteration 完成。多个测试变体（重连节点、插入干扰节点）均证实此行为。流式 API 无法提前返回，使 progressive streaming 功能完全失效。

signals.topic: Summary Index 检索功能在 Weaviate 完全失效，其他向量库部分失效
signals.summary: Summary Index 启用后在 Weaviate 上的检索完全不工作（Summary 向量消耗 top_k 槽位后静默消失），其他向量库也无法正确继承 Summary 分数。
aliases: summary score inheritance failure vector db
signals.review_reason: RAG 检索质量的核心功能完全失效，提供了精确到行号的 bug 定位和修复方案。虽然 count=1，但 bug 证据极其充分（两个 bug，四个向量库受影响，Summary 静默消耗检索配额），属于关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: Summary Index retrieval is completely broken on Weaviate (and partially broken on all vector DBs)
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供了两个具体 bug 的代码行号和修复方案。Bug1: Weaviate return_properties 缺少 is_summary 和 original_chunk_id。Bug2: str vs uuid.UUID 类型不匹配导致所有向量库的 Summary 分数继承失败。Summary 消耗了 top_k 槽位但完全不返回结果，静默失败。影响 RAG 核心检索质量。

signals.topic: Client-Server API Inconsistency: update operations accepted by client but rejected/dropped by OSS REST server
signals.summary: Python client advertises metadata-only and timestamp-only update operations as valid, but the OSS REST server returns 422 (text required) or silently drops fields, causing main update flows to fail silently or error for self-hosted deployments.
signals.review_reason: 3 related issues from the same author all about client-server contract violations: client advertises operations the server rejects (422) or silently ignores (dropped fields), plus a path prefix mismatch that blocks self-hosted users entirely. These are not edge cases — they cause main CRUD update flows to fail or silently lose data for every self-hosted deployment. P0 warranted by review_reason despite count=3, as these represent systemic API design gaps.

source_issues.title: Metadata-only memory updates are accepted by the client but rejected by the OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Client update() accepts metadata as sole parameter and sends {"metadata":{...}} to /v1/memories/{id}/ but FastAPI returns 422 because MemoryUpdate.text is required. Steps to reproduce and server code reference provided.

source_issues.title: Client `update(..., timestamp=...)` is documented as supported but the REST server rejects or drops it
source_issues.evidence: Client advertises timestamp as valid update field; timestamp-only update returns 422, and text+timestamp update silently drops timestamp. Both paths are broken.

source_issues.title: Custom `host` in the Python client cannot talk to the documented OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Client hardcodes /v1/... paths but OSS server uses bare paths (/memories, /search). Self-hosted users following integration docs get 404 on /v1/ping/ during client init, blocking all operations.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 crashes/fails when using pgvector in OSS mode
signals.summary: When openclaw-mem0 is configured in OSS mode with pgvector as the vector store, the plugin initializes but then crashes with 'Client has already been connected' errors and fails to find better-sqlite3 bindings, making memory completely unavailable for OpenClaw users with PostgreSQL backends.
aliases: Client has already been connected pgvector
signals.review_reason: Critical functionality (memory initialization, recall, auto-capture) is completely unavailable when pgvector is the configured vector store in OSS mode. Full stack trace and config provided. Blocks the main workflow for any user with a PostgreSQL-backed OpenClaw deployment.

source_issues.title: [Bug][OpenClaw][OSS/pgvector] openclaw-mem0 crashes/fails when using pgvector in OSS mode
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction config provided. Plugin registers successfully then crashes with 'Could not locate the bindings file' for better-sqlite3 followed by 'Client has already been connected. You cannot reuse a client.' from PGVector.initialize. Memory operations completely unavailable.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 userMapping config regression breaks multi-user deployments
signals.summary: The userMapping config key previously supported in v0.4.0 is rejected by openclaw-mem0 v1.0.4 schema with an 'additional properties' error, breaking privacy boundaries in multi-user/household OpenClaw deployments where different users' memories would collapse into a shared Mem0 user scope.
signals.review_reason: Explicit regression from a previously working feature (v0.4.0) in v1.0.4. Breaks multi-user privacy boundaries — a core deployment scenario — causing user identity scopes to merge. Confirmed schema-level change. P1 warranted by severity of privacy impact despite count=1.

source_issues.title: [OpenClaw] Regression: 1.0.4 rejects previously-supported userMapping config for multi-user deployments
source_issues.evidence: Explicit regression: v0.4.0 supported userMapping config key for mapping OpenClaw session keys to per-user Mem0 identities. v1.0.4 rejects this key with schema 'additional properties' error. Breaks privacy boundaries — memories from different people collapse into shared Mem0 user scope.

signals.topic: Ollama embeddings endpoint mismatch causes TypeError: fetch failed
signals.summary: Mem0 attempts to call /v1/embeddings (OpenAI-style) when using Ollama, but Ollama requires /api/embeddings. This causes the embedding layer to fail entirely with TypeError, blocking all memory operations that depend on embeddings.
signals.review_reason: Embedding layer is foundational — when it fails, no memory can be stored or retrieved because vector representations cannot be generated. Root cause clearly identified (wrong endpoint path). Complete failure of core functionality for Ollama users.

source_issues.title: mem0 plugin fails with "TypeError: fetch failed" when using Ollama – wrong embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: mem0 calls POST http://host:11434/v1/embeddings but Ollama requires /api/embeddings. Results in TypeError: fetch failed. Plugin cannot create or use embedding model with Ollama.

signals.topic: SQLite-specific database parameter causes PostgreSQL connection failure
signals.summary: openmemory API hardcodes check_same_thread=False (SQLite-only parameter) into SQLAlchemy engine initialization, causing psycopg2 to reject the connection with 'invalid connection option check_same_thread' when DATABASE_URL points to PostgreSQL.
signals.review_reason: Self-hosted users cannot connect to PostgreSQL — the database is unreachable entirely due to a SQLite-specific parameter being hardcoded in the engine initialization. Exact file, error message, and reproduction steps provided.

source_issues.title: connect_args={"check_same_thread": False} causes PostgreSQL connection to fail
source_issues.evidence: File path identified (openmemory/api/app/database.py). Exact error message: psycopg2.ProgrammingError: invalid dsn: invalid connection option 'check_same_thread'. Reproduced by setting DATABASE_URL to PostgreSQL string and starting uvicorn.

signals.topic: .NET: ToolApprovalRequestContent/ToolApprovalResponseContent reconciliation failure after session serialization/deserialization
signals.summary: Function approval workflow crashes with InvalidOperationException when session is persisted and restored between approval request and response, due to object reference mismatch after round-trip.
aliases: Tool approval reconciliation fails after session serialization
Session persistence breaks tool approval workflow
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：tool approval 是关键的人机交互机制。session 持久化是 .NET agent-framework 的官方支持特性，两者的组合路径崩溃直接破坏生产级 agent 应用的可靠性。提供了可复现的代码样本和完整堆栈，有直接用户影响证据。

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: `ToolApprovalRequestContent` / `ToolApprovalResponseContent` reconciliation failure after Session Serialization
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash with stack trace: System.InvalidOperationException: ToolApprovalRequestContent found with FunctionCall.CallId(s) 'call_cViqO50QJF92cudvsprnjpka' that have no matching ToolApprovalResponseContent. Occurs after SerializeSessionAsync/DeserializeSessionAsync round-trip in the tool approval workflow. LLM also silently ignores user rejections in some runs, producing unreliable non-deterministic behavior.

signals.topic: Python: Function-level middleware silently dropped when agents are cloned during HandoffBuilder workflow execution
signals.summary: HandoffAgentExecutor._clone_chat_agent() passes agent.agent_middleware (agent-level only) instead of agent.middleware (all types including @function_middleware), causing user-registered function middleware to never execute without any error or warning.
aliases: Function middleware lost in handoff workflow cloning
signals.review_reason: 关键工作流机制失效：HandoffBuilder 是官方支持的编排模式，function middleware 是核心扩展点。注册了 middleware 却完全静默失效会导致用户无法监控或干预工具调用行为，没有报错使问题极难排查。有可复现代码和精确根因分析，用户影响明确。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: HandoffBuilder drops function-level middleware when cloning agents
source_issues.evidence: Root cause precisely identified: _clone_chat_agent() uses agent.agent_middleware which only returns agent-level items, not @function_middleware. Includes complete reproduction code. Function middleware never fires but no error is raised — completely silent failure. Blocks any user function middleware use in handoff orchestration patterns.

signals.topic: Python: GitHubCopilotAgent does not forward provider config to Copilot SDK, making BYOK and Azure Managed Identity impossible
signals.summary: GitHubCopilotAgent._create_session() and _resume_session() never forward the provider field to the underlying github-copilot-sdk SessionConfig, blocking Azure Managed Identity, BYOK, and custom endpoint configurations.
signals.review_reason: 企业级部署阻断：Azure Managed Identity 是 Azure 上生产部署的标准认证方式，BYOK 是企业安全合规要求。GitHubCopilotAgent 无法配合这些认证方式意味着企业用户无法在 Azure 环境中使用 Copilot agent。已有本地验证的修复方案，用户影响证据充分。

source_issues.title: Python: GitHubCopilotAgent does not forward provider config to SessionConfig, BYOK not working
source_issues.evidence: Root cause precisely identified in _create_session() and _resume_session() — provider field is never forwarded to SessionConfig. Verified working locally with AzureCliCredential + Azure Managed Identity bearer token. Blocks production Azure Container Apps deployment using Managed Identity — a core enterprise Azure authentication pattern.

signals.topic: Python: AG-UI protocol fails to pass state to AgentSession, blocking ContextProvider integration
signals.summary: AG-UI implementation does not propagate state to AgentSession. Since ContextProvider relies on state to pass valid information, users cannot pass agent_id, user_id, tenant_id, etc. to HistoryProvider (which inherits from ContextProvider) when using the AG-UI protocol.
aliases: AG-UI state not passed to AgentSession
ContextProvider cannot receive state via AG-UI protocol
signals.review_reason: 关键集成路径失效：AG-UI 是 agent-framework 与前端集成的核心协议，ContextProvider/HistoryProvider 是官方推荐的上下文注入机制。两者的组合路径完全不可用使用户无法在 AG-UI 场景下注入任何业务上下文（user_id、tenant_id 等），这是生产应用的基本需求。缺乏任何 workaround。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: The current implementation of AG-UI fails to pass the state to AgentSession.
source_issues.evidence: AG-UI is a key protocol for agent frontend integration. State not reaching AgentSession means ContextProvider/HistoryProvider (the official way to inject context) is completely non-functional in AG-UI deployments. User explicitly states: 'these values cannot be effectively passed to the HistoryProvider when the frontend uses the AG-UI protocol.' No workaround exists.

signals.topic: Python: BedrockChatClient sends toolConfig.toolChoice without toolConfig.tools when agent has no tools, causing ParamValidationError
signals.summary: When an Agent has no tools configured, BedrockChatClient still sends toolConfig.toolChoice to AWS Bedrock without toolConfig.tools, violating AWS API contract and raising botocore.exceptions.ParamValidationError.
aliases: BedrockChatClient ParamValidationError when agent has no tools
AWS Bedrock API validation error on tool-free agents
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：所有不带工具的 agent 使用 BedrockChatClient 时都会立即抛出 ParamValidationError 导致请求失败。这是一个简单的条件漏检 bug，影响所有 Bedrock 无工具 agent 用户群体。提供了完整复现代码和错误堆栈，修复模式已有先例（PR #4535）。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: BedrockChatClient sends `toolConfig.toolChoice` without `toolConfig.tools` when agent has no tools
source_issues.evidence: Direct ParamValidationError stack trace: 'Missing required parameter in toolConfig: tools'. Affects any agent without tools using BedrockChatClient. Referenced PR #4535 which fixed a similar tool_choice='none' case — this is a known pattern of regression.

signals.topic: HTML report fails to render when inlined report.js contains literal </script> string
signals.summary: Playwright's HTML reporter inlines the report.js bundle directly into a <script type="module"> block. When the bundle contains a literal </script> sequence (from React DOM internals), the browser parser prematurely closes the script tag, leaving the rest of the bundle as raw text on the page and making the report entirely unreadable. Workaround is setting PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_DO_NOT_INLINE_ASSETS=1.
signals.review_reason: A confirmed bug that breaks the core HTML report UI entirely, making test reports unreadable. The reproduction is straightforward and the root cause (script tag injection) is well-documented. This directly blocks users from viewing test reports, which is a primary Playwright artifact. Count=1, but the user impact is severe (complete report unavailability), justifying P1 over P2.

source_issues.title: HTML report breaks when inlined report.js contains </script>
source_issues.evidence: Playwright's HTML reporter inlines report.js into a <script type="module"> block. The bundled report.js contains a literal </script> from React DOM internals (s.innerHTML="<script></script>"), causing the browser to prematurely close the script tag. The report UI becomes entirely unreadable, displaying raw JavaScript instead of the test report. This is a confirmed bug with a documented workaround (PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_DO_NOT_INLINE_ASSETS=1), but the workaround requires additional configuration from users.

signals.topic: connectOverCDP silently redirects all browser downloads to Playwright temp folder, causing real file loss
signals.summary: When Playwright attaches via connectOverCDP (e.g., AI browser agents, Claude Chrome extension, Playwright-MCP), it calls Browser.setDownloadBehavior globally on the entire browser context. This silently redirects ALL downloads — including those made by the human user hours later in their own tabs — to Playwright's temp folder, losing the original filenames from Content-Disposition and accumulating orphan files. User reported 2.6 GB of lost downloads accumulated over one week.
signals.review_reason: Quantified data loss (2.6 GB of files) with direct SQLite evidence from Chrome's download history DB. The root cause is well-understood: Playwright's connectOverCDP globally reconfigures download behavior for the entire browser, affecting both automation and human user's tabs simultaneously. This is a clear cost loss and privacy issue — human user downloads are silently redirected without their knowledge. Count=1 but the severity and specificity of evidence (DB query results showing file paths) is compelling enough for P1.

source_issues.title: [Feature] Opt-in to preserve browser-default download behavior when connectOverCDP attaches to a user-owned browser
source_issues.evidence: User reported discovering a 15 KB Read.ai transcript silently disappeared from ~/Downloads. Querying Chrome's SQLite download history DB showed all downloads from the past week — including a 1.4 GB video downloaded twice — had been silently redirected to /tmp/playwright-artifacts-XXXXX. The root cause: chromium.ts:_connectOverCDPImpl sets downloadsPath to artifactsDir and defaults acceptDownloads to 'accept', firing Browser.setDownloadBehavior globally for the entire browser context. 2.6 GB of orphan files accumulated because an AI browser agent had attached via CDP. This is a direct, quantifiable cost loss with concrete evidence.

signals.topic: Playwright CLI drag command fails with Zod validation error — drag-and-drop automation is non-functional
signals.summary: The playwright-cli daemon's drag command converts positional arguments into startRef/endRef but never passes startElement/endElement to the MCP tool, causing a Zod validation error on every invocation. Drag-and-drop automation via CLI is completely broken.
signals.review_reason: A confirmed, reproducible bug in the CLI tool that completely breaks drag-and-drop automation. The root cause is a simple code path issue (missing parameter passing to MCP tool). While count=1, the bug is trivially reproducible and the fix is straightforward — confirmed code-level issue in the daemon commands handler.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright CLI Drag is not working
source_issues.evidence: CLI drag command consistently fails with Zod validation error: startElement and endElement are received as undefined despite being required fields. Root cause identified in playwright-core/lib/tools/cli-daemon/commands.js: positional args are converted to startRef/endRef but startElement/endElement are never passed to the MCP tool. Every invocation fails.

signals.topic: Multithreaded Playwright Java IPC fails under high concurrency — pages fail to load or throw Unknown new child errors
signals.summary: When running Playwright Java in a multithreaded environment (one browser per sub-thread, each with its own page/context), high concurrency triggers IPC protocol errors: 'Unknown new child: tracing@...' exceptions and 'Cannot find object to call __adopt__: page@...' errors, causing scrape failures and crashes.
signals.review_reason: A confirmed bug affecting a specific use case (multithreaded Playwright Java for high-concurrency scraping). While count=1, the user is completely blocked from their production scraping workflow. The IPC protocol errors are real Java exceptions occurring in a real production environment (Netease mailanti service). P2 rather than P1 because the use case (multithreaded Playwright Java) is more specialized than the core Node.js/CLI use case.

source_issues.title: multithread IPC problem
source_issues.evidence: User runs Playwright Java (com.microsoft.playwright) with multiple threads, each creating one browser with its own page/context for scraping. Under high concurrency, the Java IPC layer throws 'Unknown new child: tracing@...' exceptions and 'Cannot find object to call __adopt__: page@...' errors. Stack traces show the failures in Connection.dispatch and PageImpl.content/navigate, causing scrape operations to fail entirely.

signals.topic: WebKit viewport setup randomly fails with Protocol error: Failed to resize window
signals.summary: On Linux (Ubuntu 25.10), launching WebKit with device emulation (e.g., 'Blackberry PlayBook') under X11 randomly fails with 'Protocol error (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride): Failed to resize window'. The failure is non-deterministic, making reliable headless browser automation with WebKit device emulation impossible.
signals.review_reason: A confirmed bug affecting WebKit device emulation, which is a supported Playwright feature. The random (non-deterministic) nature makes automated testing unreliable — tests may pass sometimes and fail others. This blocks users who depend on WebKit with specific device viewports. Count=1, random/non-blocking nature, P2.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Unable to setup viewport on webkit
source_issues.evidence: On Ubuntu 25.10 with X11, running WebKit with device emulation randomly fails with 'Protocol error (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride): Failed to resize window'. Debug logs (pw:protocol) confirm the failure. The non-deterministic nature means tests or automation relying on WebKit device emulation cannot be reliably automated, directly blocking cross-browser test coverage.

signals.topic: 缺少 Kernel 层面的审计日志钩子，导致受监管行业无法生成防篡改的操作记录
signals.summary: Semantic Kernel 缺少在 kernel 级别暴露 pre/post 函数执行钩子的机制，导致受监管行业（金融、医疗）的部署无法生成可验证的操作记录来满足 EU AI Act Article 12 等合规要求。用户在生产中被迫通过 monkey-patching 等非官方方式绕过，或依赖可被篡改的普通日志。
signals.review_reason: 3条独立 issue 均指向同一根本问题：Semantic Kernel 无 kernel 级别的审计钩子。受监管行业（金融/医疗/EU AI Act）部署因此无法生成防篡改记录，面临合规阻断风险。Issue #13813 明确说明生产环境需要但没有官方 API，需 monkey-patching。虽非崩溃级 bug，但影响受监管行业的关键合规需求（EU AI Act Article 12），有明确用户影响证据。

source_issues.title: Audit trail hooks for agent tool execution
source_issues.evidence: EU AI Act Article 12 requires automatic event logging that can be independently verified. No hook point exists for creating tamper-evident records.

source_issues.title: Audit trail for plugin/function calls
source_issues.evidence: Finance and healthcare deployments require tamper-evident records. Author states 'the kernel side doesn't expose a clean hook that downstream tooling can attach to without monkey-patching'.

source_issues.title: EU AI Act compliance scan — Semantic Kernel has the strongest human oversight
source_issues.evidence: Third-party compliance scanner found action-level audit logging only in 6 files. Author asks to validate if logging happens in production vs tests — confirms absence of formal audit trail API.

signals.topic: Google Gemini 连接器不发送 tools 字段，导致 function calling 功能完全失效
signals.summary: 当使用 AddGoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion 且配置了 FunctionChoiceBehavior 或 GeminiToolCallBehavior 时，连接器未将 tools 字段包含在 API 请求中，导致 function calling 完全不工作。相同配置在 OpenAI 兼容端点下正常，证明了问题在于 Gemini 连接器而非配置。
signals.review_reason: 明确的阻断性 bug：Google Gemini 连接器的 function calling 功能完全失效（functionCalls.Count always 0），主流程阻断。有 HTTP trace 日志证据证明 settings 被识别但未序列化进请求。虽然 count=1，但影响的是 Google Gemini 集成这一重要连接器的核心功能，用户已提供完整复现步骤，属于严重功能缺失。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion doesn't send tools/functions in API request
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed functional regression: functionCalls.Count is always 0. HTTP trace log shows settings recognized but not serialized into request. Same config works with OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

signals.topic: Ollama 连接器缺少禁用 think 模式的 SDK 暴露接口
signals.summary: Ollama 模型支持 think 模式（模型先输出推理过程再输出答案），但 Semantic Kernel 的 OllamaPromptExecutionSettings 未暴露 Think 配置选项，导致用户无法在 SDK 层面禁用该模式，必须直接使用 Microsoft.Extensions.AI 的底层 API 才能设置 OllamaOption.Think = false。
signals.review_reason: 功能缺口导致用户体验显著下降：Ollama think 模式默认开启会额外消耗 token 和延迟，用户无法通过 Semantic Kernel SDK 关闭，只能降级使用底层 API。这违反了 Semantic Kernel 提供统一抽象层的设计目标，用户被迫绕过 SDK。

source_issues.title: NET: How to disable think mode when calling the ollama model
source_issues.evidence: User shows Microsoft.Extensions.AI supports AddOllamaOption(OllamaOption.Think, false) but Semantic Kernel's OllamaPromptExecutionSettings does not expose this option. User explicitly requests: 'It is recommended to add a method like chatOptions.AddOllamaOption(OllamaOption.Think, false)'.

signals.topic: RAG 场景下 AnnotationContent 的引用标签不可读，无法追溯来源
signals.summary: 在 RAG（向量存储检索增强生成）场景中使用 Semantic Kernel 处理 Azure AI Foundry 的文件时，AnnotationContent 提供的引用标签格式为【4:6†source】，用户无法从中识别原始文档来源，缺乏文档说明，导致 AI 生成结果的溯源不可能。
signals.review_reason: RAG 场景下的关键功能不可用：引用溯源是 RAG 的核心价值，当引用标签不可读且无文档说明时，用户无法验证 AI 回答的来源，RAG 的可信度基础被破坏。Issue 已关闭（可能已修复），但需要确认是否彻底解决。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Citations not provided in AnnotationContent
source_issues.evidence: The Label is inscrutable (no documentation that I can find): 【4:6†source】. Original text from embedded chunk and location of citation in source is not provided.

signals.topic: Python SDK 无法跨插件共享上下文，导致重复生成 embedding 浪费成本
signals.summary: 用户需要将 embedding 后的向量或其他上下文数据传递给多个插件，但 Python SDK 缺乏 Kernel.Data（C# 版）的等效机制，导致每个插件各自独立调用 embedding 生成服务，对相同输入产生重复调用，造成不必要的成本消耗和延迟。
signals.review_reason: 明确的成本浪费问题：相同输入在多个插件中重复生成 embedding，浪费 API 调用配额和增加延迟。虽然影响范围限于 Python SDK 的特定使用模式，但属于架构性缺失，C# 版本有 Kernel.Data 但 Python 版本没有等效机制，跨语言能力不一致。

source_issues.title: Python: What is the alternative to Kernel.Data in C# within python implementation
source_issues.evidence: Same embedding operation performed within each plugin causing duplicate calls to embedding generation service for the exact same input query. User wants to generate embedding once outside plugins and share across multiple plugins.

signals.topic: Rate limit decode fails for unknown plan_type 'prolite'; business seat users told out of usage at 4%
signals.summary: Closed enum deserialization fails for 'prolite' plan; business seats incorrectly show exhausted at 4% — systemic rate limit display bugs.
aliases: Unknown plan type causes rate limit fetch failure
signals.review_reason: Key feature unavailable / billing anomaly: rate limit checking completely fails for users with the 'prolite' plan type due to enum deserialization error. Separately, business seat users are incorrectly told they are out of usage at 4%, suggesting systemic rate limit display bugs that can lead to unexpected service denial.

source_issues.title: codex-cli fails to decode rate-limit response when plan_type is 'prolite'

New Thread button unclickable on Win11
App cannot be relaunched after closing via X

Conversation history not persisting in desktop app

signals.topic: Auth token refresh fails — 'refresh token was already used' forces re-authentication (known recurring issue)
signals.summary: Users forcibly logged out during normal usage due to token refresh failure; referenced as duplicate of issue #9634 indicating systemic recurring problem.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: users are forcibly logged out during normal usage due to token refresh failure. Disrupts continuous workflow and automated scripts. Referenced as a known recurring issue (duplicate of #9634), indicating systemic token handling bug.

source_issues.title: Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was already used. Please log out and sign in again.
source_issues.evidence: Users are forcibly logged out with a token refresh error. Referenced as a duplicate of issue #9634, indicating this is a known recurring problem. Disrupts continuous workflow and blocks automated/scripted usage.

signals.topic: Computer tool silently drops modifier keys (keys param) on click/double_click/drag/move/scroll actions
signals.summary: The SDK's Computer and AsyncComputer action dispatch does not extract or pass the `keys` parameter from API responses, silently dropping Shift+click, Ctrl+click, Alt+drag etc. — standard desktop multi-select and keyboard-modified operations. All 5 action types affected. No error, no warning.
aliases: keys parameter missing from Computer actions
signals.review_reason: Core functionality breakage: standard desktop modifier-key operations (Shift+click multi-select, Ctrl+click new tab, Alt+drag) are silently lost. The `keys` parameter is part of the GA OpenAI API spec but the SDK never extracts or passes it. No error raised, behavior silently deviates from API contract. Users implementing computer-use agents will not discover this until their operations fail silently in production.

source_issues.title: Computer interface silently drops modifier keys (keys param) from API response
source_issues.evidence: The `keys` parameter on click/double_click/drag/move/scroll is part of the GA OpenAI computer tool API but is silently dropped by the SDK's dispatch in tool_actions.py. ActionClick(type='click', x=500, y=300, button='left', keys=['shift']) becomes click(500, 300, left) with no warning. Standard desktop operations like Shift+click (multi-select) and Ctrl+click (new tab) are broken.

signals.topic: Session persistence sanitizer strips required `id` from built-in tool-call items causing API 400 errors
signals.summary: _sanitize_openai_conversation_item unconditionally strips the `id` field from all conversation items. Built-in types (file_search_call, code_interpreter_call, web_search_call) require `id` per the OpenAI Conversations API spec, resulting in 'Missing required parameter: items[0].id' 400 errors on turn 2 when using OpenAIConversationsSession with FileSearchTool or CodeInterpreterTool.
aliases: missing required id in conversation items
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker: any agent using FileSearchTool or CodeInterpreterTool with OpenAIConversationsSession will fail with a 400 API error on turn 2. The root cause is in the SDK's own sanitizer which unconditionally removes a required field. The API spec and SDK type definitions both confirm id is required. This is not an edge case — it affects any multi-turn session with these tools. The user provided a workaround (override the sanitizer), but the SDK fix is needed.

source_issues.title: _sanitize_openai_conversation_item strips required id from built-in tool-call items
source_issues.evidence: When OpenAIConversationsSession batches turn 1 output items for add_items(), the sanitizer strips 'id' from file_search_call items. The API returns 400 'Missing required parameter: items[0].id'. Reproduction: Agent with FileSearchTool + vector store, OpenAIConversationsSession, trigger file_search on turn 1, send follow-up on turn 2. SDK type definitions confirm id is Required[str] for ResponseFileSearchToolCallParam, ResponseCodeInterpreterToolCallParam, and ResponseFunctionWebSearchParam.

signals.topic: Eager sqlite3 import breaks deployment in restricted environments (Google Cloud Run, minimal Python images)
signals.summary: The agents package eagerly imports sqlite3 at module load time. When deployed to environments like Google Cloud Run with minimal Python base images that exclude sqlite3, the import fails and the application crashes on startup with no way to use the SDK even for features that don't need sqlite3.
signals.review_reason: Startup crash that blocks deployment in common production environments. Google Cloud Run's minimal Python image does not include sqlite3. The user was blocked for over an hour before discovering the root cause. This affects any developer trying to deploy the SDK to restricted/minimal container environments without sqlite3 support. Not a beta feature — the SQLiteSession import path eagerly loads sqlite3.

source_issues.title: Don't eagerly import sqlite3
source_issues.evidence: User deployed to Google Cloud Run with default minimal Python image. App failed to start because sqlite3 is not part of the default image. User had a down server for an hour while working around by specifying --base-image 'google-24-full/python314'. The user is not using any sqlite3-dependent features but still blocked. A lazy-loading pattern was proposed.

signals.topic: Tracing truncation logic causes RecursionError when LLM response contains None values
signals.summary: BackendSpanExporter's truncation logic enters infinite recursion when processing LLM responses with None content values. The _truncated_preview() method returns a dict for NoneType, which _truncate_mapping_for_json_limit() then treats as a normal mapping, recursively re-truncating its own preview structure, causing stack overflow and hiding the original run error.
signals.review_reason: SDK crashes (not application code) during trace export, which also corrupts/obscures the original error context. Users running with tracing enabled will encounter a RecursionError instead of their actual run error. The root cause is in the SDK's truncation logic creating a self-referential loop. This is a reproducible runtime crash path.

source_issues.title: RecursionError in tracing truncation: preview dict recursively re-truncated when message content is None
source_issues.evidence: When LLM response contains content: None and the response needs truncation, the truncation logic recursively re-truncates its own preview dict (NoneType -> dict with 'truncated' key -> bool -> dict again). Stack overflow occurs in BackendSpanExporter. This hides/noises the original run error. Trigger: child_budget set to 0 on a payload containing content: None.

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when base64 file inputs are introduced, causing significant cost increase
signals.summary: When mixing text-only and file-input (base64-encoded) requests in the same conversation chain, the prompt cache hit drops to 0% even though the shared prefix (instructions, tool definitions, static content) is unchanged. Repeat file-input requests recover to ~90%, but the first file-input in a sequence always gets 0% cache. This forces users to pay full price for every new file introduction.
aliases: prompt cache invalidated by base64 files
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact: the primary value of prompt caching is reducing token costs. When a base64 file input in any position causes 0% cache hit on first introduction, users pay full price repeatedly for the same conversation context. This is not a minor UX issue — it's a significant, measurable cost leak. User provided reproducible measurement data. Note: the root cause may be at the API level (not SDK), but the issue is filed against the SDK and the user needs a workaround or confirmation from the SDK team.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: User measured cache hits across rounds: text_only_first: 96.7%, text_only_repeat: 96.7%, then file_input_first: 0.0% (unexpected, despite unchanged prefix/instructions/tools), text_only_new: 96.7%, file_input_repeat: 90.3%. User verified same behavior with Responses API directly. Estimated significant cost impact from paying full price every time a new file input is introduced. Workaround: unknown.

signals.topic: Batch API with GPT-5.x models returns 404 model_not_found error, fully blocking batch job completion
signals.summary: When using the /v1/batch endpoint with GPT-5.x models via /v1/chat/completions, the backend appends `-batch` suffix to the model name, but the batch variant does not exist, causing 100% of batch requests to fail with HTTP 404 and `model_not_found`. GPT-4o models work fine with the same code path, and /v1/responses works fine with GPT-5.x — only the GPT-5 + batch + chat/completions combination is broken.
aliases: gpt-5-batch model not found in batch API
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker for users running batch evaluation jobs: every single batch request fails with 404 and model_not_found, preventing any batch workload from completing with GPT-5 models. The failure is reproducible, has a clear error path, and directly blocks the primary use case (batch processing) for the affected model family.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Batch API returns 404 with GPT-5.x models
source_issues.evidence: Batch request_counts show completed=0, failed=2, total=2 for GPT-5. GPT-4o with same code succeeds (completed=2, failed=0). /v1/responses with GPT-5.x works fine. Root cause: backend appends '-batch' suffix for GPT-5 but the batch variant does not exist.

signals.topic: Server-side compaction not emitted during consecutive function_call-only turns, causing context overflow in agent loops
signals.summary: When using context_management compaction with Responses API, no compaction event is emitted during turns that return only function_call output. Compaction only appears once the model returns a message. In multi-turn tool agent loops with several consecutive function_call turns, context grows unbounded until context_length_exceeded is hit — before any compaction is ever seen.
aliases: compaction not triggered in tool-only responses
signals.review_reason: This directly blocks the primary use case of tool-calling agent loops: the compaction mechanism that is supposed to prevent context overflow silently fails during the most common agent loop pattern (consecutive function_call turns), causing the exact failure (context_length_exceeded) it was designed to prevent. The impact is cumulative across multiple turns, making it a repeated main-flow blocker in production agent applications.

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: Repro shows input_tokens growing from 5084→5119→5154 across consecutive function_call-only turns with no compaction item. Compaction only appears at turn 3 when the model finally returns a message. User explicitly warns this causes 'context_length_exceeded before compaction appears' in real agent loops.

signals.topic: Response.output_text and responses.parse crash when API returns output_text item with null text field
signals.summary: The SDK's strict response parsing rejects `output_text` items where the `text` field is null, causing `Response.model_validate()` to raise a validation error. Additionally, `responses.parse()` attempts structured parsing on null text entries, leading to secondary failures. This prevents users from processing Responses API payloads that contain null text fields.
aliases: Response parsing fails with null text
structured output parse crash on null text
signals.review_reason: Key parsing functionality breaks when the API legitimately returns null text fields, preventing users from processing valid Responses API responses. While the impact is conditional (only on null fields), structured output parsing is a critical path feature and this failure makes it unreliable for real-world payloads.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when an output_text item has text: null
source_issues.evidence: Repro code shows Response.model_validate() failing on a valid API payload with one output_text item having text=null. Related PR #3062 exists, confirming the bug is recognized. Affects both direct parsing and responses.parse().

signals.topic: All requests fail with 'Your request was blocked' OpenAIException when using custom API base URL
signals.summary: When initializing the OpenAI client with a custom base URL, every request returns `OpenAIException - Your request was blocked`. The same request works correctly with direct HTTP requests and with the requests library, indicating the SDK adds something (headers or behavior) that causes the proxy/gateway to block the request. This fully blocks all API usage for custom endpoint users.
aliases: request blocked with custom base URL
signals.review_reason: Complete functional failure for all users with custom API base URLs (e.g., Azure, proxies, internal deployments). Every request is blocked, making the SDK unusable in these environments. While the issue is closed, the evidence shows a persistent SDK-level behavior difference vs direct HTTP that blocks the primary workflow for affected users.

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – "Your request was blocked" with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: Issue author confirms: same request works with direct HTTP/requests library, works with litellm (same issue), but fails only with the openai-python SDK. All requests blocked — complete functional failure for custom base URL use case. 4 comments on the issue indicate ongoing discussion.

signals.topic: Persistent sessions: sessionDir field always null causes prompt command to fail with 'No acpx session found'
signals.summary: When creating persistent sessions, the session index JSON is written with `sessionDir: null`. This breaks the `prompt` subcommand (and likely `exec` continuation) because these commands resolve the session directory using the null field, while `status` and `sessions` commands read the index directly and work fine. Users see 'No acpx session found' even though the session is registered.
aliases: prompt command fails to find existing session
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: the prompt command — a core ACPX workflow — is completely broken for persistent sessions. Users cannot resume or continue existing sessions despite them being registered in the index. This is a direct code bug (null pointer in sessionDir field), not a configuration or UX issue.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions: sessionDir is null, prompt cannot find session
source_issues.evidence: Session index JSON written with sessionDir: null. status and sessions commands work (read index directly), but prompt fails because it needs the actual session directory path. Error: 'No acpx session found (searched up to /home/user/workspace)'

signals.topic: --no-wait flag causes queued prompts to never be processed; jobs silently lost
signals.summary: When submitting a prompt with the `--no-wait` flag (fire-and-forget mode), the job is accepted into the queue and the CLI returns a job ID, but the queue owner process never processes the queued job. The session shows as running but no work is done. Regular (blocking) prompts work fine, confirming the queue owner is alive but the IPC queue consumer is deadlocked.
signals.review_reason: Core workflow failure: the `--no-wait` fire-and-forget mode silently drops prompts — the user gets a job ID confirmation but no work is ever done. This is not a UX confusion but a confirmed deadlock/bug in the IPC queue consumer path. The workaround (`--timeout`) indicates the queue owner is alive; the bug is in how the queue consumer picks up jobs.

source_issues.title: [BUG] --no-wait queues prompt but queue owner never processes it
source_issues.evidence: acpx --approve-all codex --no-wait 'Create /tmp/test.txt' returns [queued] <job-id> immediately, but file is never created. Queue owner process is alive (confirmed via ps aux) and regular prompts work fine. Workaround: use --timeout instead of --no-wait. This means prompts submitted via IPC queue path are silently lost.

signals.topic: WSL environment passes Linux-style cwd paths to Windows .exe agents, causing session/new to fail
signals.summary: When ACPX runs on WSL2 and spawns a Windows .exe agent (e.g., copilot.exe), the cwd passed to `session/new` is a Linux POSIX path (e.g., `/home/user/.openclaw/workspace`). Windows agents validate paths using their own filesystem and reject Linux paths with 'Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed'. This blocks any ACP session from being established in a WSL→Windows agent cross-environment setup.
aliases: WSL2 Windows agent cwd validation failure
wslpath -w needed for Windows exe agents
signals.review_reason: Interoperability workflow failure: a specific but real environment combination (WSL2 + Windows .exe agents) completely blocks ACP session establishment. The root cause is clearly identified (POSIX cwd not converted via wslpath -w). The workaround requires manual path conversion. Affects users who have Windows agents accessed from WSL, a documented and common setup.

source_issues.title: WSL→Windows cwd path translation when spawning Windows .exe agents from WSL
source_issues.evidence: acp-client's asAbsoluteCwd() always produces a POSIX path on Linux/WSL, sent directly to Windows agent via session/new. Windows agent returns: {"error": {"code": -32603, "data": {"details": "Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed: /home/user/.openclaw/workspace"}}}. Tested: Linux paths fail, native Windows C:\ paths work, WSL UNC \\wsl.localhost\ paths work. WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows 11, Copilot CLI v1.0.20 Windows binary.

signals.topic: CLI --session flag silently ignored in exec mode, causing repeated 'No acpx session found' errors
signals.summary: When a user (or AI agent) uses `acpx <agent> --session <name> "prompt"`, the --session flag is silently ignored because exec mode does not use sessions. The command falls back to one-shot exec mode and fails with 'No acpx session found' — which is confusing because the user explicitly provided a session name. This leads to wasted time and API credits from repeated failed attempts.
aliases: CLI UX confusing for AI agents
wrong acpx command form silently falls back to exec
signals.review_reason: UX/API usability issue causing repeated workflow failures and wasted API credits. Although only 1 issue is reported, the author explicitly describes making the same mistake 3 times in a row, and the silent flag ignore pattern is a systemic design problem that likely affects other users and agents. The core issue (prompt not respecting --session flag) is a valid pain point even at count=1. Not P0 because it is not a code-level block — the workaround (correct command form) is available and documented.

source_issues.title: CLI command structure is extremely confusing for AI agents — acpx claude vs acpx claude prompt vs acpx claude exec
source_issues.evidence: Author (AI agent) tried `acpx claude --session e4f29a00 'prompt'` three times before discovering the correct form is `acpx claude prompt --session xxx 'prompt'`. Each failed attempt wastes API credits. The --session flag on the top-level command is silently dropped in exec mode with no error or warning. Issue closed without a fix — labeled as UX design problem.

signals.topic: Skill scanner produces widespread false positive 'Suspicious' flags on legitimate skills
signals.summary: At least 11 skills are incorrectly flagged as 'Suspicious' by the OpenClaw scanner despite passing VirusTotal (0/65) and/or OpenClaw's own Benign verdict. The scanner's static analysis patterns misfire on common legitimate behaviors (env var access, file I/O, network calls). This undermines trust in ClawHub's security labeling and forces skill authors to file false-positive disputes.
signals.review_reason: 11 distinct skill authors report false suspicious flags. Multiple skills pass both VirusTotal and OpenClaw's own Benign criteria yet still display a 'Suspicious' banner. This directly degrades trust in ClawHub's security review system and blocks legitimate skill distribution. Issue #1618 identifies a systemic root cause: the scanner's registry summary doesn't preserve env var/credential fields from SKILL.md, causing systematic mismatch for any credential-requiring skill.

source_issues.title: [False Positive] olostep skill flagged as Suspicious — OLOSTEP_API_KEY correctly declared in metadata.openclaw
source_issues.evidence: Scanner reads registry summary which has no fields for env vars/credentials/homepage, causing mismatch vs SKILL.md. Systemic issue confirmed across venice-api-kit, firecrawl-search, aikek, getpost-scrape. Only zero-credential skills pass. OpenClaw verdict: Benign (medium).

source_issues.title: [False Positive] verdikta-bounties-onboarding v1.4.1 — both scanners report Benign
source_issues.evidence: Both VirusTotal and OpenClaw scanners return Benign. OpenClaw assessment confirms all five criteria pass. Static patterns (env var + network, file read + network, child_process) are inherent to the skill's declared blockchain agent functionality.

source_issues.title: False Positive: Memory Never Forget v3.2.1 incorrectly flagged as Suspicious
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw scan explicitly states Benign (high confidence). Skill is 100% local, no credentials, no external calls. False positive triggered by normal local file I/O patterns.

source_issues.title: False positive: neuro-humble skill flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Instruction-only pedagogical skill. VirusTotal shows no detections. Flag likely triggered by clinical/disability-justice content rather than actual security risk. Initial automated scan correctly identified it as internally consistent.

source_issues.title: Skill flagged as 'Suspicious' despite VirusTotal 0/65 — possible VT status parsing issue
source_issues.evidence: VirusTotal shows 0/65 detections for both v6.0.4 and v6.1.0. OpenClaw scanner confirms Benign (high confidence). ClawHub likely reads wrong field from VT response (e.g., community score) instead of engine detection count.

source_issues.title: 我的技能被标记了可疑，请查实后解除可疑标记：auto-backup-openclaw-user-data
source_issues.evidence: Skill author (MIT open-source project) disputes suspicious flag. Skill uses Node service for backup, which the scanner may misidentify.

source_issues.title: wolverine-ai skill flagged as suspicious — requesting guidance
source_issues.evidence: Skill is a supervised crash recovery wrapper. Authors already removed external API references, reframed language, added safety controls (rate limiting, loop guard, backups). Cannot determine specific trigger.

source_issues.title: ClawHub Security flagged skill as suspicious (zhongguo-nongli-huangli-jixiong)
source_issues.evidence: Author requests review and guidance on what triggered the flag.

source_issues.title: [False Positive] Skill 'userorbit' flagged as suspicious - Request for Review
source_issues.evidence: Skill updated to v1.1.1 fixing all prior flagged concerns (moved to env vars, explicit metadata, removed auto-created files). Still showing suspicious flag despite resolution.

signals.topic: GitHub OAuth login flow broken — users cannot sign in to ClawHub
signals.summary: Multiple users report that signing in with GitHub fails after OAuth authorization. The page refreshes without completing authentication, blocking access to the platform. Affects both new registrations and re-registrations after account deletion.
signals.review_reason: Three independent users are completely blocked from signing in — the primary entry point to the platform. Both new users and re-registration attempts fail. This is a clear primary-flow blocker with high user impact.

source_issues.title: Cannot signin. First time trying to publish

source_issues.evidence: User cannot login from web UI or CLI (clawdhub login). Cleared cache, tried Chrome and Safari, revoked and reconnected GitHub token — all attempts fail with generic 'Sign in failed. Please try again.' message.

signals.topic: Plugin/Skill search broken — returns Server Error
signals.summary: The Plugins search feature on ClawHub returns a 'Something went wrong Server Error' for all queries. Multiple users in different browsers are affected, making the skill discovery feature completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Key discovery feature (skill/plugin search) is entirely broken across all users. While only one issue is reported, server errors in search are commonly under-reported because users give up. This directly degrades platform usability for finding skills.

source_issues.title: Error when using Plugins search: Something went wrong Server Error
source_issues.evidence: User sees server error screenshot for all plugin searches. Confirmed across multiple browsers and after logging in/out. Plugin search is completely broken.

signals.topic: Skill publishing update causes duplicate skill entries and inability to delete
signals.summary: A skill update inadvertently split the published skill into two separate entries. The user has no way to delete the duplicate, leaving the skill marketplace with incorrect listings.
signals.review_reason: A version update split a single skill into two entries with no way for the author to remove the duplicate. This creates a poor marketplace experience with duplicate listings. While impacting only one user so far, broken versioning behavior tends to affect other authors similarly.

source_issues.title: Skill flagged — suspicious patterns detected (processon-diagram-generator)
source_issues.evidence: User updated a version and it created two distinct skill entries. Asks how to delete one of them. No delete mechanism provided.

signals.topic: Resume token invalid across separate tool calls breaks approval gate workflows
signals.summary: When a Lobster pipeline pauses for approval and returns a resumeToken, using that token in a subsequent tool call fails with 'Invalid token' or 'Invalid pipeline resume state', making approval gates unusable in multi-call workflows.
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow-blocking bug. The resume token's entire purpose is to be used later, but it fails across separate tool invocations. Users must avoid approval gates entirely as workaround, which removes a core gating mechanism. Reported with full repro steps, two error modes, and a plausible root cause hypothesis.

source_issues.title: lobster resume: token invalid across tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Pipeline pauses with needs_approval + resumeToken; subsequent lobster resume --token <token> call fails with 'Invalid token' (inline mode) or 'Invalid pipeline resume state' (file mode). Both inline and .lobster file modes tested, same agent session. Hypothesis: resume state stored in gateway process memory, not persisted to disk.

signals.topic: No per-step timeout causes workflows to hang indefinitely on hung steps
signals.summary: Lobster provides no mechanism to set timeouts on individual steps. A hung curl, unresponsive LLM provider, or blocking script holds the entire workflow forever, with no way to fail fast or recover.
signals.review_reason: No timeout mechanism means any single hung step blocks the entire workflow indefinitely. Documented scenarios (LLM provider degradation, unresponsive API, blocking scripts) are realistic production failures. Combined with on_error policy, timeout would enable recovery rather than full workflow halt — the absence of this is a clear capability gap in reliability-critical workflows.

source_issues.title: Per-step timeout with on_error integration
source_issues.evidence: LLM provider outages cause llm.invoke to hang for minutes; network API calls without explicit -m flags wait indefinitely; no timeout on shell scripts; workflow SLA violations for interactive triage; ctx.signal is passed through but no timeout signal is created. This blocks the entire workflow from completing.

signals.topic: Any step failure halts entire workflow with no partial failure recovery
signals.summary: When any step fails, the entire Lobster workflow stops unrecoverably. There is no on_error policy to continue past failures, making multi-source monitoring, notification fan-out, and cleanup workflows brittle.
aliases: workflow halts on any step failure
signals.review_reason: Single point of failure in error handling prevents real-world production workflows from operating resiliently. Multi-source and fan-out scenarios are documented as production use cases, and the inability to continue past a failure is a significant reliability gap.

source_issues.title: Per-step on_error handling for partial failure recovery
source_issues.evidence: Multi-source monitoring: if one source is down, entire dashboard update halts. Notification fan-out: Slack failure prevents email delivery. Cleanup workflows: one provider failure prevents cleanup of remaining providers. No way to record which steps failed or continue with partial data.

signals.topic: Workflows are strictly sequential with no parallel execution support
signals.summary: Lobster workflows run all steps sequentially. Independent steps like fetching from GitHub, Jira, and Slack run one after another, taking 3x wall-clock time compared to parallel execution, directly impacting interactive triage SLA.
signals.review_reason: Sequential execution of independent steps causes significant wall-clock overhead. Multi-source polling is described as a core use case, making this a real performance pain point for latency-sensitive workflows. Not P0 because it is not workflow-blocking, but a clear experience degradation.

source_issues.title: Parallel step execution for concurrent branch workflows
source_issues.evidence: Multi-source aggregation is a documented core use case. A monitoring workflow polling 5 sources every 5 minutes spends most time waiting on sequential network calls. Wall-clock time directly impacts interactive triage workflows where humans wait for results.

signals.topic: No LLM cost tracking or spending limits causes budget overruns
signals.summary: llm.invoke receives token usage data but it disappears through the pipeline. Teams discover LLM cost overruns from billing alerts, not from the tool. A 5-LLM-step workflow run every 5 minutes can cost $144–$1,440/day with zero visibility.
aliases: no spending limits on LLM calls
signals.review_reason: Hidden LLM costs represent a real financial risk. Automated workflows calling LLMs repeatedly with no cost visibility can incur significant unexpected charges. The cost model is quantified ($144–$1,440/day), making this a concrete operational concern rather than speculative.

source_issues.title: LLM cost tracking and spending limits
source_issues.evidence: Token usage data from LLM responses flows through pipeline and disappears. Workflow with 5 LLM steps can cost $0.50–$5.00 per run; running every 5 minutes = $144–$1,440/day with no visibility. Teams discover overruns from billing alerts, not proactively.

signals.topic: Windows: ollama launch openclaw creates duplicate gateway process when Scheduled Task is already running
signals.summary: On Windows with Gateway running as a Scheduled Task (Session 0), running `ollama launch openclaw` fails to detect the existing gateway process due to Session 0 isolation, spawning a second node.exe that binds to the same port 18789. This causes mDNS name conflicts, RPC probe failures, EPERM errors on pending.json writes, and handshake timeouts — completely blocking the gateway workflow for affected users.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-blocking bug on Windows when using Scheduled Task mode. Session 0 isolation prevents `ollama launch openclaw` from detecting the already-running gateway, causing duplicate processes to compete for port 18789. The resulting symptoms (mDNS conflict, RPC failures, EPERM file errors, handshake timeouts) are severe and directly block the main gateway workflow. Workaround requires running PowerShell as Administrator to kill the duplicate process manually. Affects any Windows user who has the gateway installed as a Scheduled Task.

source_issues.title: [Windows] ollama launch openclaw starts duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: user-session processes cannot enumerate Session 0 processes. Symptoms include: Bonjour mDNS name conflict 'DESKTOP-xxx (OpenClaw) (2)', 'RPC probe: failed', EPERM errors writing to ~/.openclaw/devices/pending.json, mass handshake timeout / gateway closed (1006) errors. No automatic detection of existing gateway via port 18789 or Scheduled Task state.

signals.topic: Windows Tray App fails to auto-reconnect after Gateway restart, leaving node permanently disconnected
signals.summary: When the OpenClaw Gateway restarts, the Windows Tray App (Node Mode) does not automatically reconnect and stays in a disconnected state indefinitely. The CLI node correctly implements automatic reconnection logic, but the Tray App lacks this, forcing users to manually toggle Node Mode off and on to recover — a significant UX regression compared to the CLI.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear UX regression: the Windows Tray App fails to auto-reconnect after a Gateway restart, leaving the node permanently disconnected with no automatic recovery. Unlike the CLI node which correctly implements reconnection retry logic, the Tray App silently stays disconnected and requires manual intervention to recover. This directly impacts node availability for all Tray App users whose gateways restart — a scenario that is common during updates, crashes, or gateway restarts. The workaround of manually toggling Node Mode is non-obvious and degrades the user experience significantly.

source_issues.title: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart
source_issues.evidence: After Gateway restart, Tray App logs show 'Node status changed: Disconnected' with no subsequent reconnection attempts. CLI node logs show correct behavior: 'Node reconnecting in 1000ms (attempt 1)'. Tray App requires manual toggle of Node Mode off/on to recover. Reporter is running Tray App 0.4.7 on Windows 11 x64 with remote Gateway over WSS (Nginx TLS reverse proxy).

signals.topic: Circuit breaker fails to block ping-pong tool loops — agents get stuck in infinite loops consuming CPU and API budget
signals.summary: The globalCircuitBreakerThreshold blocks individual tools but not their ping-pong pairs, so agents can switch to the unblocked partner tool and restart the loop indefinitely, rendering loop detection ineffective.
aliases: loop detection ineffective for paired tools
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is indefinitely blocked. The loop detector fires but the circuit breaker does not actually halt execution — agents successfully restart the loop on the alternate tool. This causes unbounded CPU and API token consumption with no recovery. Concrete log evidence provided showing the cycle repeating indefinitely.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: globalCircuitBreakerThreshold blocks per-tool, not per-pair — ping-pong loops survive circuit breaker
source_issues.evidence: Agents in ping-pong loops (e.g. memory_search ↔ memory_get) bypass circuit breaker by switching to the unblocked partner tool, continuing indefinitely. Logs show CPU pegged at 36% with loop cycling indefinitely.

signals.topic: macOS companion node fails to execute commands — system.run.prepare missing in companion binary
signals.summary: OpenClaw macOS companion app lacks the system.run.prepare command, causing all exec host=node commands to fail silently on Mac targets.
signals.review_reason: Key cross-platform management feature is completely broken for macOS targets. The exec host=node command is a primary use case for the companion node, and it fails silently with no workaround. Clear user impact: users cannot control their Mac from OpenClaw.

source_issues.title: macOS companion node missing system.run.prepare breaks exec host=node
source_issues.evidence: Users with macOS companion node cannot execute commands from OpenClaw on their Mac; the companion binary is missing the system.run.prepare handler that the gateway requires for exec host=node.

signals.topic: Isolated cron sessions fail to spawn when main session is inactive — cron automation unreliable
signals.summary: agentTurn cron jobs intermittently fail to launch when the main session has been idle, timing out with no sessionId or token usage, making scheduled automation unreliable.
aliases: cron job fails after main session idle
signals.review_reason: Cron-based automation (a core reliability feature) is intermittently unavailable with no user recourse. Jobs fail silently — no session is even created — after long wait times, wasting user time and breaking automated workflows. Regression: this behavior did not occur previously.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron job sessions fail to spawn after main session inactivity
source_issues.evidence: Isolated cron jobs fire and wait 6–17 minutes, then report 'cron: job execution timed out' with no sessionId and no token usage — indicating the isolated worker never launched. Failure is correlated with main session inactivity; jobs succeed when main session is active.

signals.topic: Remote Control UI behind reverse proxy requires pairing even with valid gateway token — remote access blocked
signals.summary: Users deploying OpenClaw behind Traefik (or similar reverse proxies) cannot authenticate to the Control UI using a valid gateway token; it always shows 'pairing required' or 'origin not allowed'.
aliases: Control UI auth behind reverse proxy
origin not allowed proxy token auth
gateway token not accepted via Traefik
signals.review_reason: Remote access via the Control UI is completely blocked for reverse-proxy deployments — a primary deployment pattern for self-hosted users. The UI cannot authenticate even with a correctly provided gateway token, forcing users to expose the gateway directly or abandon remote UI access entirely.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Remote Control UI behind Traefik still shows pairing required with valid gateway token on v2026.4.9
source_issues.evidence: Gateway logs show 'token_missing' and 'unauthorized: gateway token missing' even when correct token is provided, and 'Proxy headers detected from untrusted address'. The Control UI is completely inaccessible via reverse proxy despite correct configuration.

signals.topic: Telegram voice notes not transcribed — audio pipeline not triggered for voice messages
signals.summary: Telegram voice notes do not enter the STT/transcription pipeline at all; no transcript is produced and no chat message is injected, despite proper STT config.
aliases: audio pipeline not triggered for Telegram voice
signals.review_reason: A major Telegram use case (voice messages) is completely non-functional. Users cannot send voice notes — a common accessibility and convenience feature — with no error indication. The issue is not in the STT provider but in the message routing layer that promotes Telegram voice to the media pipeline.

source_issues.title: Telegram voice notes do not trigger STT/transcription pipeline on v2026.4.9
source_issues.evidence: Voice notes sent from Telegram produce no log lines for audio, voice, transcrib, media, ogg, or opus — the audio is silently ignored before reaching the STT pipeline, despite STT config being present and Telegram text messages working.

signals.topic: Desktop app fails with 'Path not found' error when using Ollama/LMStudio local models

source_issues.evidence: 用户在桌面应用中配置 Ollama 后无法启动 Agent 交互，终端可正常工作但桌面应用报 Path not found 错误，主流程完全阻断。

signals.topic: LiteLLM third-party model cost mapping warnings pollute output for Qwen/DeepSeek users
