signals.topic: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError crashes on Windows consoles (cp1252 / block characters)
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught UnicodeEncodeError when printing Unicode block characters (\u2588) on Windows terminals using cp1252 encoding, blocking the entire tool from running.
aliases: Windows console Unicode block character crash
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (#5012, #5001) both show uncaught UnicodeEncodeError on Windows. The error occurs during core output operations (lint messages, console printing), completely crashing aider. This is a main-flow blocker on Windows platforms. Count=2 meets threshold.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError when printing lint warning messages on Windows cp1252 console. The \u2588 block character cannot be encoded, crashing the entire application. Affects lint_edited code path.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in utils.py line 139
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in utils.py during console output, same root cause (Windows cp1252 encoding cannot handle certain Unicode characters).

signals.topic: Uncaught RuntimeError crashes on symlink loops
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught RuntimeError when encountering circular symlinks during repo map file resolution, blocking core functionality.
signals.review_reason: Single issue but demonstrates clear main-flow crash during repo map generation. The symlink loop case is a common scenario in dotfiles/repo setups. While count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence (app completely crashes during init).

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1237
source_issues.evidence: Aider crashes during get_repo_map() → get_all_abs_files() → safe_abs_path() when resolving paths with symlink loops (e.g. dotfiles with circular symlinks). Uncaught RuntimeError propagates to top level, crashing the app during repo scan.

signals.topic: Uncaught PermissionError crashes on cache directory creation at startup
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught PermissionError when it lacks write permission to create its cache directory, preventing the tool from starting.
signals.review_reason: Single issue but clear startup blocker. The PermissionError during cache dir creation prevents the entire tool from starting. Affects users in Docker/non-root environments. Strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1311
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError when trying to create /app/.aider/caches directory. Occurs during check_version() at startup, completely blocking aider from running. Docker/non-root environment scenario.

signals.topic: Uncaught OSError crashes when argument or file path is too long
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught OSError when command-line arguments exceed OS path length limits, causing aider to treat argument strings as file paths and crash.
aliases: OSError File name too long crash
Long system message argument path crash
signals.review_reason: Single issue but clear crash path. The issue shows the tool misinterprets long argument strings as file paths and crashes. Main-flow blocking for affected users.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 842
source_issues.evidence: When a --system-message argument value exceeds OS path length limits, Path(all_files[0]).is_dir() crashes with OSError [Errno 36]. Affects users who use very long system messages.

signals.topic: Uncaught NotImplementedError in /read-only command on Windows with absolute glob patterns
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught NotImplementedError when using the /read-only command with absolute glob patterns on Windows, blocking the command from functioning.
signals.review_reason: Single issue but specific Windows crash in a named command. The /read-only command completely crashes on Windows when using absolute patterns. Platform-specific main-flow blocker.

source_issues.title: Uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py line 1090
source_issues.evidence: NotImplementedError raised when cmd_read_only runs Path(root).glob(expanded_pattern) with a non-relative pattern on Windows. Crashes the /read-only command entirely.

signals.topic: redteam discover command fails with Unknown task error, blocking target discovery workflow
signals.summary: The `promptfoo redteam discover` command sends an unrecognized `target-purpose-discovery` task name to the promptfoo.app remote API, resulting in HTTP 400 on every request. This makes the entire target discovery feature completely unusable for any user, despite `redteam generate` working with the same credentials and endpoint.
signals.review_reason: The `redteam discover` command is completely non-functional due to an invalid task name sent to the remote API. This is a primary workflow blocker for any user attempting target discovery in red team evaluations. Although count=1, the review_reason provides explicit evidence of full feature blockage with no workaround, warranting P1 (not P0 due to single-instance evidence).

source_issues.title: `promptfoo redteam discover` fails with `Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery`
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 Bad Request on every `redteam discover` call; server explicitly rejects `target-purpose-discovery` as an invalid task name. No workaround available. The feature is entirely non-functional.

signals.topic: Node.js engine incompatibility prevents installation and startup of latest promptfoo
signals.summary: Node.js v22.21.1 (the current LTS range) is incompatible with the latest promptfoo 0.121.3 due to engine requirements of `^20.20.0 || >=22.22.0`. Installation fails with ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE, preventing users from running redteaming commands entirely.
signals.review_reason: Node.js engine incompatibility causes complete inability to install or start promptfoo for users on the v22.21.x range. This is a startup-level crash that blocks the entire tool. Count=1 with explicit engine mismatch evidence and crash stack trace.

source_issues.title: Unable to install latest version of promptfoo
source_issues.evidence: npm EBADENGINE error: required node `^20.20.0 || >=22.22.0`, current node `v22.21.1`. Crashes at runtime with ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE, blocking all promptfoo usage including redteaming. No immediate workaround described.

signals.topic: Provider config isolation failure — max_tokens leaks across providers causing API 403 errors in multi-provider evals
signals.summary: When running a multi-provider eval with both older and newer OpenAI models, max_tokens config set on one provider leaks to other providers that do not define it. This causes HTTP 403 errors on newer models (e.g., gpt-5.4-mini) that reject max_tokens and require max_completion_tokens, resulting in eval failures.
signals.review_reason: Provider config isolation failure causes API 403 errors that prevent multi-provider evaluations from completing. Users must resort to running separate eval commands per provider as a workaround, which is a significant degradation of core multi-provider eval functionality.

source_issues.title: max_tokens config leaks across providers in multi-provider eval
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 403 errors on gpt-5.4-mini API calls caused by max_tokens leaked from gpt-4.1-mini config. Explicit reproduction steps provided with working config. Only workaround is running each provider in separate eval commands.

signals.topic: TypeScript providers fail when importing other .ts files — transitive imports resolve as undefined
signals.summary: TypeScript providers that import other .ts files from the project fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Promptfoo only transpiles the provider file itself but not its transitive .ts dependencies, which then go through Node's native module resolution and fail.
signals.review_reason: TypeScript provider transitive import resolution failure breaks a common pattern where users share project code between their app and eval providers. A workaround exists (tsx + NODE_OPTIONS) but requires an additional dependency and defeats the purpose of 'native TypeScript support' marketing. Low-frequency but real user impact when using TypeScript-based providers.

source_issues.title: TypeScript provider fails when importing other .ts files from the project
source_issues.evidence: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND error when provider imports another .ts file from the project. The 'native TypeScript support' claim is misleading because only the entry provider file is transpiled, not its dependencies. Workaround requires tsx dependency and NODE_OPTIONS flag.

signals.topic: Assertion type 'not-javascript' fails to reject function/object/number value types — tests silently pass when they should fail
signals.summary: The `not-javascript` assertion type does not properly handle all value types. When assertion.value is a function, object, or number (not just boolean), the assertion incorrectly passes instead of failing. This means tests that should reject code containing these value types pass silently.
signals.review_reason: The 'not-javascript' assertion silently passes when it should fail for non-boolean value types, causing false negatives in red team and security test suites. This undermines the reliability of assertion-based evaluations by allowing dangerous code to pass tests without warning.

source_issues.title: assertion type: "not-javascript" doesn't work in all cases
source_issues.evidence: Assertion with type: 'not-javascript' and value as a function/object/number passes when it should fail. Root cause identified in handleJavascript() — inverse check only handles boolean type. Silent incorrect pass undermines test reliability.

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore sync methods crash in ASGI environments and break connection pooling
signals.summary: ElasticsearchStore wraps all sync methods via asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(), which causes RuntimeError ('Future attached to a different loop') in ASGI deployments (Gunicorn+Uvicorn) and prevents shared connection pooling across requests. Two separate issue reports confirm this.
aliases: ElasticsearchStore pooled clients different event loop error
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm that ElasticsearchStore is completely non-functional in ASGI environments (Gunicorn+Uvicorn) — a mainstream production deployment pattern. The 'attached to a different loop' error and inability to pool clients are runtime-blocking failures that prevent production use. This is not a degraded-mode issue; the entire sync path is broken.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore sync methods use run_until_complete — breaks in ASGI with pooled clients
source_issues.evidence: asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete() causes RuntimeError in ASGI; pooled AsyncElasticsearch client bound to one event loop; two separate issue reports with identical root cause

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore sync methods use run_until_complete — breaks in ASGI with pooled clients
source_issues.evidence: metadata_keyword_suffix ignored on sync path + ASGI runtime errors from run_until_complete; sync-to-async bridge fundamentally broken

signals.topic: Bedrock streaming calls silently never retry on transient errors due to @retry_decorator on async generator
signals.summary: The _conversion_stream_with_retry function in Bedrock is decorated with tenacity's @retry_decorator, but since it uses 'yield' it is an async generator. Tenacity cannot intercept exceptions during async generator iteration — only the initial call (which merely creates the generator object) is wrapped. Retries never fire for ThrottlingException or ServiceUnavailableException.
aliases: Bedrock streaming retry never fires async generator decorator
tenacity retry decorator async generator silent failure bedrock
signals.review_reason: This is a critical reliability defect: the retry mechanism on Bedrock streaming is completely inert — it never fires under any circumstances because the decorator cannot intercept exceptions in async generators. AWS throttling and service unavailability are common transient errors in production, and users will experience repeated failures instead of automatic retries. The silent nature (no error on decorator application) makes it especially dangerous as users may be unaware their streaming retry protection is gone.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @retry_decorator on async generator _conversion_stream_with_retry is silently inert
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows yield makes the function an async generator; tenacity's retry only wraps the initial call which creates the generator object; no code runs and no retry ever fires for streaming calls with ThrottlingException or ServiceUnavailableException

signals.topic: ImageBlock/AudioBlock/VideoBlock resolve methods crash on second call — breaking change from PR #20743
signals.summary: PR #20743 introduced a regression where calling resolve_image/resolve_audio/resolve_video twice raises ValueError: resolve_image returned zero bytes, because the buffer pointer is never reset to 0. The previous behavior (v0.14.15) correctly returned the buffer on repeated calls.
aliases: ImageBlock resolve_image crashes second call ValueError
buffer pointer not reset breaking change v0.14.16
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression from a recent PR that introduces a breaking change: calling resolve methods twice now crashes the application with ValueError. The reproducer is exact and unambiguous. Any workflow that processes the same block twice (e.g., re-indexing, retries, multi-pass pipelines) is completely broken. This is a main-flow failure affecting anyone on >=0.14.16.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Breaking Change in Message Block Buffer Resolution
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows v0.14.15 correctly returns buffer on repeated calls; v0.14.16 raises ValueError on second call; clear regression introduced in PR #20743 affecting ImageBlock, AudioBlock, VideoBlock

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore.query() ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on synchronous path — metadata filters silently misbehave
signals.summary: The synchronous wrapper for ElasticsearchStore.query() does not forward metadata_keyword_suffix to aquery(), causing custom metadata suffix configurations to be silently ignored. The sync path always falls back to the default .keyword suffix.
aliases: sync query path wrong metadata suffix aquery
signals.review_reason: Metadata filter queries on the sync path silently produce wrong results when users have custom metadata suffixes — this is not a crash but a data correctness defect. Users performing filtered retrieval will get incorrect or incomplete results without any error signal. The async path works correctly, making this a clear inconsistency between sync and async code paths.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore.query() ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on the synchronous path
source_issues.evidence: Explicit bug report: synchronous wrapper does not forward metadata_keyword_suffix; only the async path (aquery) honors the parameter; users with custom metadata suffixes get silently wrong query results

signals.topic: DocumentSummaryIndex.delete_nodes() crashes with KeyError on invalid node IDs instead of skipping them
signals.summary: delete_nodes() mutates its input list during iteration (to filter invalid IDs), which causes some invalid IDs to be skipped in the iteration and remain in the list. Those are then passed to delete_nodes() which does a raw dict lookup, raising KeyError. The expected behavior is to skip invalid IDs silently.
aliases: list mutation during iteration delete nodes crash
signals.review_reason: A clear algorithmic bug where the fix is trivial (use a separate list instead of mutating during iteration) but the impact is real: any attempt to delete non-existent nodes causes an unhandled KeyError crash. Users cleaning up stale nodes in mixed valid/invalid ID scenarios will experience unexpected crashes.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: DocumentSummaryIndex.delete_nodes() crashes on invalid node IDs instead of skipping them
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer provided: calling delete_nodes(['does_not_exist_1', 'does_not_exist_2']) raises KeyError because list mutation during iteration causes invalid IDs to not be filtered before dict lookup

signals.topic: ESM/CJS regression: autopilot and claims commands crash with 'require is not defined' on fresh install
signals.summary: Fresh 3.5.75 installs contain bare require() calls inside compiled ESM modules, causing autopilot status/enable/disable/config/reset/log/learn/predict/check and claims list to crash immediately with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined'. No workaround; user had to resort to session-start hook sed patches.
signals.review_reason: count=4, all independent reports of the same crash on fresh install. ALL autopilot subcommands and claims list are completely broken. Users have no working workaround besides fragile sed patches re-applied on every npm install. This is a primary workflow blocker: users cannot use core v3 features at all on a fresh install.

source_issues.title: [Bug] `ruflo autopilot` and `ruflo claims` fail on fresh 3.5.75 install -- bare `require()` calls inside ESM modules
source_issues.evidence: Fresh npm install -g ruflo@latest: both ruflo autopilot status and ruflo claims list crash with ERROR require is not defined. Core v3 features completely broken on first use.

source_issues.title: ESM/CJS regression in 3.5.75
source_issues.evidence: ruflo autopilot status and ruflo claims crash with ERROR require is not defined on fresh 3.5.75 install.

source_issues.title: Bug: bare require() calls in ESM modules cause 'require is not defined' on autopilot/claims commands (v3.5.75)
source_issues.evidence: Same crash: ruflo autopilot status and ruflo claims list crash with ReferenceError: require is not defined. Severity High. User workaround is sed patch re-applied on every npm install.

source_issues.title: Bug: autopilot commands fail with 'require is not defined' (CJS in ESM package)
source_issues.evidence: ALL autopilot functionality broken: status, enable, disable, config, reset, log, learn, history, predict, check all fail. MCP path also fails: mcp__claude-flow__autopilot_status returns -32603: require is not defined.

signals.topic: Data destruction: init/cleanup/bridge commands silently overwrite or delete user config files without backup
signals.summary: Three separate commands silently destroy user data: (1) init --skip-claude overwrites global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with a 4-line stub without backup; (2) cleanup --force deletes entire .claude/ directory including user-owned agents, skills, settings, memory.db, git worktrees; (3) bridge.curateIndex() overwrites hand-curated 14KB MEMORY.md with a 1-line stub on every assistant turn tick.
signals.review_reason: count=3 with explicit data-loss evidence across three distinct commands. All three are silent (no confirmation prompt, no backup) with user-visible permanent data destruction. The curateIndex() issue is especially severe: fires on every assistant turn, silently nuking 14KB of user documentation for an unknown period. The cleanup --force issue destroys settings.local.json that can take hours to curate. These are critical user pain points.

source_issues.title: init --skip-claude overwrites ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md without backup
source_issues.evidence: init --skip-claude (promised to skip .claude/ dir) silently overwrote user's 42-line global CLAUDE.md with 4-line auto-generated stub. No backup created. Permanent data loss of workflow rules and session hooks.

source_issues.title: cleanup --force deletes entire .claude/ directory including user-owned Claude Code config
source_issues.evidence: npx ruflo@latest cleanup --force deleted entire .claude/ directory: custom agents, skills, slash commands, settings.local.json (hours of work), memory.db, git worktrees, launch.json. Dry-run misleadingly showed .claude/ as a single line implying it belongs to ruflo.

source_issues.title: bridge.curateIndex() overwrites hand-curated MEMORY.md with stub (@claude-flow/memory@3.0.0-alpha.12, alpha.13)
source_issues.evidence: curateIndex() fires on every Stop hook tick (end of every assistant turn) and silently overwrites 14KB hand-curated MEMORY.md with single-line stub. 17 hand-curated sections permanently lost. Recovery only possible via backend snapshots.

signals.topic: MCP tool failures: agent_spawn blocked by schema mismatch; code-intelligence tools return empty results from stub implementations
signals.summary: agent_spawn always fails with 'type: Required' schema validation error blocking all agent lifecycle via MCP. All 5 code-intelligence MCP tools (semantic-search, architecture-analyze, refactor-impact, split-suggest, learn-patterns) return empty results because core helper functions are stubbed. WASM modules reference non-existent packages.
signals.review_reason: count=3, all independent reports of MCP tool breakage with concrete evidence of user-facing impact. agent_spawn is a primary workflow tool for spawning agents and is completely blocked with no workaround. Code-intelligence MCP tools silently return empty results, making them useless without any error signal.

source_issues.title: agent_spawn MCP tool fails with 'type: Required' -- SpawnAgentSchema/validate-input field mismatch

source_issues.title: plugin-code-intelligence: stub implementations prevent MCP tools from returning real results

signals.topic: process.cwd() misuse breaks MCP tool state persistence on Windows and ignores CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD environment variable
signals.summary: MCP tools use process.cwd() directly for storage paths. On Windows, this resolves to C:\Windows\System32 (read-only), causing all state writes to fail with EPERM. Memory commands ignore CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD, breaking Claude Desktop MCP integration with silent 'Database not found' errors. Launchd daemon wrapper uses stale bundled path after rename, silently running stale code.
signals.review_reason: count=3 with platform-specific (Windows) and integration-specific (Claude Desktop) impact. Issue 1577 is a complete block on Windows MCP usage. Issue 1562 silently misleads users into thinking their memory data is lost. Issue 1565 causes silent stale-code execution. All three have clear user-facing symptoms.

source_issues.title: MCP tools use process.cwd() which resolves to System32 on Windows
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, process.cwd() resolves to C:\Windows\System32 for AI coding agents launching MCP via npx. All 16+ MCP tool files that write state fail with EPERM: operation not permitted. All MCP tool state persistence completely broken on Windows.

source_issues.title: [Bug] memory commands ignore CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD -- bare process.cwd() breaks MCP memory tools under Claude Desktop
source_issues.evidence: ruflo memory list returns [ERROR] Failed to list: Database not found even when CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD is explicitly set. Claude Desktop MCP integration broken: end user sees 0 entries across all namespaces. Silent data-loss appearance despite data existing.

source_issues.title: Daemon update (launchd wrapper bug)
source_issues.evidence: Users who set up launchd-managed daemon before ruflo rename are silently running stale code after upgrades. Token bloat from duplicate @claude-flow/cli registration wastes 10-30K tokens per session.

signals.topic: Daemon processes accumulate as zombies with no cleanup; multiple instances run simultaneously causing 3x memory/disk/CPU overhead
signals.summary: ruflo daemon start accumulates zombie Node.js processes across sessions. daemon stop does not catch older instances. User observed 3 daemons running simultaneously for the same project, each running duplicate map/audit/optimize/consolidate/testgaps workers, resulting in 3x disk I/O, 3x SQLite writes, 3x RAM (100-140MB each), plus race conditions on shared state. Slowly degrades machine over time.
signals.review_reason: count=2, both describing zombie process accumulation and daemon cleanup failures. Issue 1551 has concrete multi-daemon evidence with measurable resource overhead (3x I/O, 3x RAM). Issue 1552 compounds the problem by adding zombie accumulation from hung one-shot commands. Together they cause continuous machine degradation.

source_issues.title: Daemon processes accumulate as zombies on v3.5.75 -- daemon stop does not clean older instances
source_issues.evidence: Multiple daemon start invocations accumulate as zombie Node processes, each holding ~100-140MB resident memory. daemon stop does not catch older instances. 3 daemons observed simultaneously for same project: 3x disk I/O, 3x SQLite writes, 3x RAM usage, plus race conditions.

source_issues.title: CLI one-shot commands (memory store, memory retrieve) hang indefinitely after completing
source_issues.evidence: ruflo memory store and retrieve print [OK] Data stored successfully but process never exits, requiring manual kill. Multiple invocations accumulate zombie Node processes. Data is written correctly but non-zero exit makes it appear as failure in automated pipelines. Automation scripts hang or timeout.

signals.topic: Recording context does not inherit HTTPS error-ignore and other session-scoped CDP settings
signals.summary: When `AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS=true` is set, the main browser context ignores certificate errors correctly. However, the recording context created by `agent-browser record start` does not inherit this or other session-scoped settings (user-agent, color-scheme). This causes `goto` to time out on self-signed HTTPS pages in recording mode, blocking headless visual verification of local development servers (e.g., mkcert).
aliases: recording context HTTPS ignore not inherited
session-scoped CDP settings not applied to recording
signals.review_reason: Silent setting drift across contexts causes recording workflows to fail on self-signed certs without error indication. This blocks a real product workflow (ProofShot local dev verification) and indicates systemic design risk for any future session-scoped CDP setting.

source_issues.title: Recording context does not inherit --ignore-https-errors / AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS
source_issues.evidence: Main context: `open https://self-signed.local:3000` works fine. After `record start`: `goto https://self-signed.local:3000` times out. ProofShot workflow blocked.

source_issues.title: Centralize session-scoped CDP settings to prevent drift across contexts
source_issues.evidence: Documents that user_agent, color_scheme, and ignore_https_errors are not re-applied to recording context. Two independent launch-time settings silently break in recording.

signals.topic: --auto-connect: duplicate Chrome remote-debugging permission prompts
signals.summary: When using `--auto-connect` to attach to an existing Chrome instance with UI remote-debugging enabled, Chrome shows two separate permission prompts: one during legacy discovery/probing (`/json/version`, `/json/list`) and another for the real websocket attach. This is caused by the code probing legacy endpoints before trying the exact DevToolsActivePort websocket path. Affects user experience on every connect attempt.
signals.review_reason: UX friction on every connect attempt to existing Chrome. Users must dismiss two prompts instead of one. While not a workflow blocker, it is a persistent and annoying regression in the remote-debugging workflow.

source_issues.title: Prefer DevToolsActivePort websocket path first in --auto-connect to avoid duplicate remote-debugging prompts
source_issues.evidence: Issue describes two separate permission prompts on Chromium 146 with UI remote-debugging. First during legacy discovery, second for websocket attach.

source_issues.title: Is it normal to always have to allow twice when connecting to an existing Chrome instance via --auto-connect?
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly asking if double-prompt is expected behavior on v0.25.3.

signals.topic: Profile sessions: active page lost and falls back to about:blank after first command, with WebSocket connection reset
signals.summary: When using `--profile` to persist sessions, the first `open` succeeds but subsequent commands (e.g., `tab list`, `get url`) lose the active page and report `about:blank`. Daemon logs show 'WebSocket Error: Connection reset without closing handshake', indicating the CDP session is dropped between invocations. Session persistence is broken for users relying on profile directories.
signals.review_reason: Breaks the core session-persistence workflow — the primary advertised use case for `--profile`. The page is confirmed loaded but the CDP session becomes unreachable after the next command, making multi-step automation impossible.

source_issues.title: `--profile` sessions lose the active page after the first command and fall back to `about:blank`
source_issues.evidence: WebSocket connection reset after first command; page target confirmed present in Chrome immediately after `open` but lost on next invocation. Daemon log: 'WebSocket Error: WebSocket protocol error: Connection reset without closing handshake'.

signals.topic: Containerized environment: CDP connection closes after login form submission, blocking entire test workflow
signals.summary: In Kubernetes-deployed containerized environments, after filling login credentials and clicking the sign-in button, the CDP connection closes with 'Failed to send CDP command: Trying to work with closed connection'. The subsequent `wait` command for the dashboard fails. This is a main-flow block — authentication flows cannot complete in CI/container contexts.
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow block in a common deployment context (Kubernetes containers). Users cannot complete login-based automation pipelines. The connection is severed mid-workflow, not merely degraded.

source_issues.title: Unable to complete the test in containerised env due to ✗ Failed to send CDP command: Trying to work with closed connection
source_issues.evidence: CDP connection drops immediately after clicking sign-in button. Workflow stops at 'wait dashboard' step. User tried --no-sandbox, --disable-dev-shm-usage, disabling shim — none resolved the issue.

signals.topic: Linux: session state (cookies and localStorage) saved but not restored across restarts
signals.summary: On Linux with v0.24.1, both `state save` and `--session-name` auto-persistence write a valid state file containing cookies and localStorage entries, but relaunching with `--state <file>` or `--session-name` restores neither. This blocks the core authenticated-automation workflow: users cannot reuse login sessions across agent-browser invocations.
signals.review_reason: Explicitly breaks the documented session/authentication reuse workflow. The write path succeeds but the restore path silently fails — users have no indication their auth state was not restored.

source_issues.title: Linux v0.24.1: state save/--state and --session-name write state but do not restore cookies or localStorage
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows saved JSON contains expected cookie and localStorage entries, but after relaunch with --state the eval returns ls:null, cookie:''. Blocks authenticated agent automation as documented.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google-vertex@4.0.106 unconditionally sends streamFunctionCallArguments to Vertex unary API, causing 100% of generateText/generateObject calls to fail with HTTP 400
signals.summary: Google Vertex provider v4.0.106 (released 2026-04-09) unconditionally adds streamFunctionCallArguments to ALL unary generateContent requests, even when no tools are present. The Vertex API rejects this parameter on unary endpoints, causing 100% failure rate for all generateText/generateObject calls across all Vertex models. Users must pin to v4.0.105 as workaround.
aliases: Google Vertex provider breaks all unary API calls in v4.0.106
streamFunctionCallArguments causes 400 on Vertex unary endpoint
signals.review_reason: Breaking regression: v4.0.106 published to npm on 2026-04-09 causes 100% of all Vertex unary API calls to fail. Every user of @ai-sdk/google-vertex is blocked from using generateText/generateObject unless they downgrade. This is a complete main-flow failure with clear user impact evidence and a working workaround (pin to 4.0.105).

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex@4.0.106: unconditional streamFunctionCallArguments breaks all Vertex unary API calls
source_issues.evidence: 100% of generateText/generateObject calls fail with HTTP 400 'streaming function call is not supported in unary API'. All Vertex models affected (gemini-2.5-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash-preview, etc.). Reproduced with Bun and Node.js. Workaround requires pinning to v4.0.105.

signals.topic: Race condition in runToolsTransformation: flush closes toolResultsStream before async transform registers outstanding tool result, causing tool executions to silently fail
signals.summary: In runToolsTransformation, the outstandingToolResults counter is incremented after an await parseToolCall(). The flush() function can fire during that await, see outstandingToolResults.size === 0, and close the toolResultsStream prematurely. Tool results are then silently dropped with 'Tool execution aborted', even though the tool executed successfully. Observed consistently in Bun v1.3.11.
aliases: stream closes during async transform causing tool result loss
outstandingToolResults race condition in tool execution
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure with silent data loss: tools execute but their results are silently dropped. User sees 'Tool execution aborted' error without understanding why. Observed consistently in Bun v1.3.11, likely affects other runtimes with non-sequential transform/flush ordering. High user impact in agentic workflows relying on tool results.

source_issues.title: Race condition in runToolsTransformation: flush closes stream before async transform registers tool
source_issues.evidence: Trace evidence shows tool executes successfully but result has nowhere to go because toolResultsStream was already closed. Silent failure — tool returns 'Tool execution aborted' with no clear signal to user. Reproduced consistently in Bun v1.3.11; may also affect other runtimes with non-strict transform/flush serialization.

signals.topic: onFinish callback silently ignored in ToolLoopAgent.stream() and generate() since v6.0.135 due to incorrect removal in PR #13698
signals.summary: PR #13698 removed experimental callbacks but also incorrectly removed the non-experimental onFinish callback from ToolLoopAgent methods. The callback is still defined in ToolLoopAgentSettings types but is never passed to the underlying streamText/generateText calls. Users expecting onFinish to fire (e.g., for logging, analytics, cleanup) silently get nothing since v6.0.135.
aliases: onFinish silently does nothing since v6.0.135
signals.review_reason: Clear regression since v6.0.135 affecting all ToolLoopAgent users who rely on onFinish callback. The callback silently does nothing — no error, no indication to user that their callback is not being invoked. Impacts common post-processing patterns (logging, analytics, cleanup) in agentic workflows.

source_issues.title: Bug: `onFinish` callback not working in `ToolLoopAgent.stream()` since v6.0.135
source_issues.evidence: Regression since v6.0.135. Working in v6.0.116, broken in v6.0.135-v6.0.157. onFinish is defined in types but never passed to streamText/generateText. Silent failure — no error, just no callback execution. Affects users relying on onFinish for post-processing (logging, metrics, cleanup).

signals.topic: export type在'use server'文件中被错误注册为Server Action（v16.1.x regression），导致构建错误或运行时ReferenceError
signals.summary: Next.js v16.1.0+中，PR #86296重构后，'use server'文件中的`export type`被错误地注册为Server Action，在编译时被registerServerReference处理，但由于TypeScript擦除了类型，运行时实际为undefined。小型项目静默错误，大型项目（使用Turbopack action聚合）出现'Export X does not exist'构建错误或ReferenceError。v16.0.3正常。
aliases: export type in use server incorrectly registered as Server Action
export type causes ReferenceError in use server files v16.1.x regression
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：v16.1.x regression导致所有在'use server'文件中使用export type的项目面临运行时ReferenceError或构建失败，在Turbopack大型monorepo中影响尤为严重。两条独立issue证实，根因已定位到PR #86296的post-pass缺少type-only检查。

source_issues.title: `export type` in "use server" file incorrectly registered as Server Action (v16.1.x regression)
source_issues.evidence: 两条独立issue（#92461 open，#92460 closed as invalid）报告同一问题，提供了详细根因分析：PR #86296的server_actions.rs post-pass未检查is_type_only。v16.1.5验证复现，v16.0.3正常。小型项目：registerServerReference(undefined)静默错误；大型项目（galaxus.ch）：Turbopack action聚合产生'Export X does not exist'构建错误。

source_issues.title: `export type` in "use server" file causes runtime ReferenceError in v16.1.x (regression from PR #86296)
source_issues.evidence: 补充运行时ReferenceError证据：export type被作为Server Action注册但类型被TypeScript擦除，导致运行时'Foo is not defined'。提供了v16.1.5验证和v16.0.3对比。workaround：将export type移出'use server'文件。

signals.topic: Turbopack在生产构建时向SWC插件传递错误的NODE_ENV（hardcoded 'development'）

Turbopack NODE_ENV hardcoded development in prod builds

source_issues.title: Turbopack passes "development" to SWC plugins during next build
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供了完整的对比表：Webpack prod构建正确传递'production'，Turbopack prod构建错误传递'development'。有源代码定位（turbopack-ecmascript-plugins/src/transform/swc_ecma_transform_plugins.rs#L240-241有TODO注释）。生产案例：galaxus.ch翻译插件因hardcoded dev环境生产构建多打包了1.4MB未拆分的翻译字典。

ChunkLoadError in Turbopack dev server on Windows pnpm

signals.review_reason: Core CI/CD workflow is broken: users relying on source control filters to conditionally run tasks get zero task execution even when changes exist. This is a direct regression of a core feature used in automated pipelines.

source_issues.title: Filtering by source control changes doesn't detect changes
source_issues.evidence: turbo run <command> --filter="[origin/main..HEAD]" does not pick up changes that git show origin/main..HEAD correctly detects. --affected flag works around this.

signals.topic: Turbo >2.8.14 cannot connect to self-hosted remote cache with custom CA certificates

source_issues.title: Dirty .gitignore causes gitignored files to leak into task input hashes (v2.8.18+)

signals.topic: Turbo build fails on Windows when using Bun as package manager due to spawnSync UNKNOWN error

turbo.exe blocked by Windows on Bun installs

The error occurs at the entry point of turbo's execution (spawnSync), preventing any turbo task from running. source_issues.title: Bun run build failed on window on fresh turbo repo

signals.topic: Timed-out tasks do not flush logs, making it impossible to identify which task failed in CI
signals.summary: When a turbo task times out, all its logs are silently dropped instead of being flushed. Users cannot determine which task timed out or what progress it made, severely hindering CI troubleshooting.
aliases: no logs for timed out tasks in CI
signals.review_reason: CI reliability issue: when tasks timeout, users are left with zero debugging information. In a monorepo with many parallel tasks, identifying which task hung is impossible without log flushing. This happens frequently enough in the reporter's CI to cause 'havoc'. Directly impacts the core value proposition of turbo's task orchestration in CI environments.

source_issues.title: Tasks that time out are not flushing logs
source_issues.evidence: In a GitHub Actions CI run, a task timed out but no logs were produced for the timed-out task. The task never even started from turbo's perspective (log group never opened).
